8.15: Deprived of hU kingdom king B&hu went to the forest followed by his wife. In his unbearable misery he put an end to his life.
8.16: His pregnant wife hailing from the family of Yadus followed him. O sinless ones, previously poison had been adminis* tered to her by her co-wife.
8.17: This co-wife arranged the funeral pyre of their commcm husband in the forest and ascended it. O brahmins, Aurva, the descendant of Bhrgu, protected her sympathetically.
8.18: The child in the womb came out along with the poison at the hermitage and thus the mighty king Sagara was bom.
8.19: Aurva performed the post-natal and other rites for the child. He taught him Vedas and Sistras. Thereafter, he taught him the mode of wielding miraculous weapons.
8.20: Thereafter, he resolved to exterminate Sakas, Yavanai, Kambojas, Paradas and Pahlavas.
8.21: Being slaughtered by that heroic noble Sagara they sought shelter in Vasitha after submitting to that learned sage.
8.22: Vasitha the extremely brilliant sage offered them free¬ dom from fear on certain conditions. He then restrained Sagara.
8.23: On hearing the words of his preceptor and being faithful to his promise Sagara suppressed their traditional rituals and changed their guise.
8.24: He released Sakas after shaving half of their heads. He completely shaved off the heads of Yavanas and Kambojas.
8.25: The Paradas were made to keep their tresses untied and the Pahlavas were asked to grow moustaches and beards. They were deprived of Vedic studies and the chanting of Va;a}kkra Manras by that noble king.

9.2: Formerly, Atri performed a great penance for three thou¬ sand divine years. So we have heard.
9.3: His semen attaining the state of Soma juice rose up. Water exuded from his eyes in ten directions and illuminated t ten quarters.
9.4: The ten delighted goddesses of the quarters conceived that foetus. They hrid it collectively but they were unable to do so any longer.
9.5: When the ten quarters were unable to uphold the foetus, it fell down to the Earth along with them.
9.6: On seeing Soma fallen to the esirth, Brahmi, the grand¬ father r£ the worlds, made him ride in a chariot for the welfare of the worlds.
9.7: O excellent sages, when the son of Atri the noble sage fell down, Devas, the sons of Brahma, and others eulogised him.
9.8: His splendour that exuded reached the Earth and turn* ed into the medicinal herbs whereby the universe is sustained.
9.9: Lord Soma acquired refulgence through the eulogies and holy rites. The highly blessed lord performed penance for hundred thousand billion years.
9.10: After acquiring that extensive realm, Soma the most excellent of those who possess gentleness performed the Rajasuya sacrifice with hundreds and thousands of gold pieces as sacrificial gifts.
9.11: O bralimins, we have heard that Soma distributed the three worlds as gifts to those important brahminical sages who had assembled there for sacriftce.

9.14: After attaining this rare prosperity coveted even by the sages, his intellect, O dear ones, whirled. In his impudence tactlessness too clouded his intellect.
9.15: Although repeatedly requested by Devas and celestial iies he did not hand over Tiri back to AAgiras.
9.16: Thereupon, the battle between Devas and Asuras en¬ sued. It became known as Tirakamaya battle. The battle raged furiously causing destruction of the worlds.

9.18: Then Brahmk himself restrained Rudra and Ufanas and handed over Tara back to Ahgiras.
9.19: She went to a forest of Iika reeds and expelled the foetus. Immediately after the birth that lordly child seized the bodies of Devas.

22.1: He who commits peijury, he who speaks with partiality and he who utters falsehood falls into Raurava hell.
22.2: O excellent sages, he who destroys a foetus, he who murders his preceptor, he who slays cows and he who aufibcates •others—all these fall into terrible Raurava hell.
22.3: He who drinks wine, he who slays a brahmin, he who steals gold and he who comes into contact with these—all these fail into Sukara hell.
22.4: He who murders a king, a Vaiiya and a royal soldier, he who defiles the bed of his preceptor and he who indulges in:sexual intercourse with his sister—all these fall into Taptakumbha hell.
22.5: He who performs a sacrifice on behalf of a person not entitled to that privilege, he who foretells by studyii stars and he who partakes of sweet cooked food all by himself falls into Krmipuya hell.
22.6: O brahmins, the brahmin who sells lac, gravy, gingelly seeds and salt falls into the same hell.
22.7: O excellent brahmins he who rears or eats poultry, goats, pigs and birds falls into the same hell.
22.8: Those who hunt wild goats, sheep, or deer fall into hell Vahnijviia. O brahmins, they too who bum things that fliould not be burnt, fall into hell.
22.9: He who commits omissions in the observance of holy
22.10: These arc the main hells* there are hundreds, and thousands of similar hells where the perpetrators of heinous crimes arc cooked by day and night and tortured.
22.11: These sins and thousands of similar sins are atoned for by men who are brought to suffering to one or other of these hells.
22.12: Those who act contrary to the tenets of disciplined life of Varias and Airamas mentally, physically or verbally, fall into these hells.
22.13: The gods in heaven are seen by the people of hells with their heads directed above. The gods see the residents of hells far below, their heads directed below.
22.14: There are as many dwellers in hell as there are crea¬ tures in heaven* He who commits sins but is avene to expiate for them, falls into hell.
22.15: Holy rites of expiation have been mentioned by great sages in proportion to sins. They have mentioned them being fully aware which particular expiation is capable of quelling the particular sin.
22.16: O leading brahmins, Manu and other sages have men¬ tioned rites of atonement—elaborate ones if the sin is elaborate and minor ones if the sin b minor*
22.17: The acts of expiatims are in the nature of austerities or holy rites. Of all of them the remembrance of Sri KrffA it the mostefiective*
22.18: Remembering Vifu at dawn, night, diuk or midday the man attains Vifpu because his sins are immediately quelled.
22.19: By remembering Vifu his pains and strains perish immediately and they attain absolution. Attainment of heaven is an obstacle Into him.
22.20: O leading brahmins, the benefits such as attaining the status of Indra as a result of Japa, Homa, worship etc are obstacles to a man whose mind is set on Vuudeva.
22.21: Hence, no brahmin, no man, who remembers Vifnu day and night, falls into hell. If he has incurred sins they perish immediately.

27.1: O sages you listen to what I am going to say now. It is a splendidancient traditiozul account connected with the Vedas. It grants worldly pleasures and salvation.
27.2: O brahmins by committing sins or performing holy rites in that subcontinent a man necessarily attains the fruit thereof whether auspicious or inauspicious,
27.3: O excellent brahmins, in that Varya, a person of self- control attains everything viz. virtue, wealth, love and libera¬ tion.
27.4: O excellent brahmins, Indra and other Devas have attained the status of a deity after performing splendid holy rites in that sub-continent.
27.5: Those persons who are devoid of ailments and who stay in heaven with aerial chariots had previously performed splen¬ did holy rites in that land of Bharata and had attained heaven thereby.
27.6: Li$tcn, O brahmins, the Bharaca sub*continent has nine sub>divisions which are separated by oceans. They are equal to one another.
27.7: In the east of it, the Kir&tas stay. The Yavanas stay in the west. O brahmins, the Brahmins, Ktriyas, Vaiiyas and Madras stay in the middle.
27.8: That spot of land to the north ofSahya where the river Godavari flows is the most charming in the entire earth*
27.9: What men do cannot be doat by Devas and Asuras. Men are engaged in holy rites while Devas and Asuras are eager to obviate their Karman.

29.1: O excellent brahmins, understand even as they are being recounted, the procedure of water libation of worship, de¬ votion to the Sun-god, and the faith as well as concentration of mind.
29.2: He who narrates the story of the lord with devotion, he who wonhips him, he who maintains the holy fires, is called the eternal devotee.
29.3: He who praises or permits the holy rites that are per¬ formed for the furtherance of the Vedas, O brahmins, is the real devotee. He is realty a great man.
29.4: The man who performs the holy rites of the Sun is a devotee of the higher type. But he should not censure other deities nor be jealous of the devotees of those deities.
29.5: The man who constantly remembers the Sun-god whether staying or moving about, whether sleeping or waking, while smelling or keeping the eyes closed or open is indeed the greatest devotee.
29.6: Purity of mind, good conduct and due observances slnild be applied to everyone. Whatever b performed with.|Rmty of mind becomes fruitful.
29.7: The devout man who circumambulates the Sungod circumambulates in effect the whole of the earth consisting of seven continents.
29.8: If a man keeps Sungod in his mind and circumambul¬ ates ether, know that Devas have been circumambulated by him.
29.9: He who makes perpetual offerings of lamps to temples,, quadrangles and highways shall become blessed and handsome.
29.10: The first preference should be given to lamps with ghee. The second preference should be given to the juices of medi¬ cinal herbs. It should never be offered with the extracts from fat suet or bones.
29.11: The lamp shall always bum with the flame leaping upwards. It shall never be directed downwards. Thus the person who offers lamps becomes refulgent. He shall never attain the state of an animal.
29.12: The burning lamp should never be taken away nor should it be destroyed. The remover of a burning lamp may attain imprisonment, destruction, wrath or darkness.
29.13: He who offers everything along with its ancillaries together with the libation of water at the time of sunrise, en- •dowed with faith, is liberated from all sins.
29.14: He who offers water-libation accompanied by gold, -cow, bull, plot of land or cloths will derive benefits lasting for seven births.
29.15: The libation of water shall be assiduously offered into €he fire, water, atmosphere, clean ground, idol or ball of rice.
29.16: The libation of water shall not be offered to the left or right. It shall be offered straight in front along with ghee andGuggula (Aromatic resin) by one who is endowed with devotion to Sun-god.
29.17: By performing libation with milk the devotee 15 never afflicted by mental distress.
29.18: By offering an umbrella banner canopy, flagstaff and chowrics to Sun-god with faith* one will attain his desired, goal.
29.19: Whatever article a man dedicates to Sun-god with devotion will be returned to him by Sungod a hundred thou¬ sand times more.

30.2: He makes the living beii shrink. He creates them once again. With his rays he illuminates and scorches the earth. He causes rain too.
30.3: They say that at the time of creation, the entire uni¬ verse is evolved from Sun-god and at the time of dissolution reverts to him.
30.4: Abandoning their abode—the physical body—innumei able Yogins turn into gaseous state and retire to Sungod who is a mass of refulgence.
30.5: Just as the birds of sky resort to the branches of treesi the sages and the liberated souls along with the gods resort to his thousands of rays and stay there.

30.21: As a matter of fact the whole of the three worlds is one unit. Himself unembodted, he is present in all the bodies.
30.22: He has the extremities of feet, hands, eyes, heads and mouths all round; he has cars all round; he stands enveloping everything.
30.23: The sole, eternal Being, holds the title Mahapurufa. Endowed with Sattva quality, intelligence and efficiency he creates his own soul by his own self.
30.24: By his own soul he creates many souls hundredfold, a. thousandfold, in hxmdred thousands, in crores.
30.25: Just as the water that falls fms firmament undergoes a change in taste by virtue of diverse tastes present in the Earth so also the soul undergoes change in attributes due to its. various contacts.
30.26: Just as the singular air within the body functions as five organic airs, so also the supreme Being has tinity and diversity undoubedly.
30.27: Just as a single lamp lights up thousands of lampS) so also he, though single, gives birth to thousands of forms.
30.28: When he realizes his self he becomes alone and single. When singleness dissolves, diversity and multiplicity begin to function.
30.29: O excellent sages, the unmanifest consisting of three attributes originated from him. That which is tintnanifest, that the form of which is not clear, is called primordial nature.
30.30: The embodied beings who are present in heaven make obeisance to him. Thereby, O celestial sage, they attain the benefit and goal as directed.
30.31: Devas who have assumed different forms, who are stationed in their respective stages of life, devoutly worship that primordial Being. He bestows salvation on them.
30.32: Those who are sanctified by him resort to the sole and single entity. This is a further achievement unto them that they enter the sole and single entity.
30.33: Thus, O N&rada, the secret doctrine has been narrat¬ ed to you. O celestial sage, by virtue of your devotion to tis the greatest fact has been revealed u> you.

38.1: Then, with thousands of clusters of flames, the Are originating from his eye burned immediately the spouse of Rati together with his attendants.

40.1: O excellent brahmins, on seeing the virility of Siva hus, Dakfa joined his palms in reverence and bowed down. Then he began to eulogise.
40.2: Obeisance to you, O lord of the chiefs of Devas, Obei¬ sance to you, O slayer of Bala, O lord of Devas, you are the most excellent one in strength, you are worshipped by Devas and Danavas.
40.3: Devas are procreated by Sv&has and Svadhau. To those who attain death Svfthas and Svadhas are offered. Svahi, Svadhit and Ahar eulogise you.
40.4: You are identical with all. You are the omnipresent lord, the lord of all living beings, and the immanent soul in all living beings. Hence you have not been invited.
40.5: O lordi you alone are worshipped in sacrifices with:.yanou8 lortt gifts. You aiooe are the doer of everything. Hence you have not been invited.
40.6: Or O lord, I have been deluded by your subtle MayL Tor that reason too, you have not been invited by me.
40.7: O lord of Devas, be pleased with me. You alone are my refuge. You are the goal and the foundation. It is my opinion that no one else is so.
40.8: After eulogising the great lord thus the highly intelli- gent Dak 9 a stopped. The delighted lord spoke to Daksa once again.
40.9: O Dakfa of good holy rites, I am delighted with this hymn of yours. Of what avail is much talk? You will come to my presence.
40.10: After uttering the words of consolation the omniscient lord of the three worlds spoke the following words succinctly put in good sentences.
40.11: O Dakya, you should not feel sad by this destruction of sacrifice. O sinless one, I am the destroyer of sacrifice and this has been seen by you formerly.
40.12: O one of Good holy rites, accept this boon from me. Wear a happy and pleasant face and listen to me attentively.
40.13: O Patriarch, by virtue of my favour, you will derive the fruit of a thousand hone and a hundred Vajapeya sacrifices.
40.14: Afler saying this to Dak of unmeasured splendour the lord of Devas vanished along with his wife and attendants.

40.16: O sages convenant vrith virtue! for dogs it is the obstruction of the vision; for horses it is the entanglement with the cavity. For peacocks it is the splitting of tlir tuft-like flower on the head.
40.17: O sages conversant with virtue, such are the fevers among living beings. It occurs at the time of birth, death and in the intervening period.

41.1: On hearing the story mentioned by Brahmi, the leading sages were delighted. Their hairs stood on ends. They praised the lord.
41.2: On hearing their words, the fburiaced lord of worlds recounted that holy centre of lord 3iva which yields worldly pleasures and salvation on this voy earth itself.
41.3: O excellent brahmins, in the previous Kalpa, there was a single Mango tree there by which name, the holy centre came to be known as Ekamra.
41.4: It contained massive doorways arranged in groups of three. A white outer wall enhanced its beauty. It was well guarded by weapons and beautified by moats and trenches.
41.5: The people were gay and joyous in perpetual festivities with various kinds of musical instruments such as Che lute, Sute and drums. The area was adorned with slings fcM* hurling missiles.
41.6: There were many temples of gods embellished by outer walls and gardens. The ways of worship therein were wonder¬ ful and they enhanced the beauty of the holy centre.
41.7: The men too were richly endowed with their noble traits and bedecked in all ornaments. They appeared to be haughty by virtue of their youth and handsome features.
41.8: O excellent sages, they were brahmins, Ktriyas, Vaijyas and 8udras. Those who lived there were very virtuous and engaged in their respective profession.
41.9: These beautiful women, pleasing to behold were experts in conversation and side-glancing at people. None of them was bereft of beauty, none harassed others, none could be called wicked or evil in their activities.
41.10: The intelligent people who visit the lord at any time, are liberated from their sins. They go to the world of lord Siva.
41.11: The holy centre extending to two and a half Yojanas to the West, East, North and South of the lord is an area that yields worldly pleasures and salvation.
41.12: Even a woman, O leadii brahmins, attains the benefit if she worships in due faith. No doubt need be entertain¬ ed in this respect.

43.1: O brahmins, formerly, in the Krtayuga there was a glorious king who was known as Indradyumna. He was as valor¬ ous asIndra.
43.2: While that king, the repository of good qualities, ruled over the Earth he thought of propitiating Visnu.
43.3: "How shall I propitiate Visjriu, the lord ofDevas? In which holy centre or sacred spot or the river bank or hermitage shall it be?"
43.4: The king went there accompanied by his flourishing army and vehicles. He duly performed a horse sacrifice where much wealth was distributed as gift.
43.5: The city of Avanti 1 in Malava, known as the most excellent one over the earth, was the capital of that monarch.
43.6: They were liberal donors of jewels and the enjoyers of riches. O excellent sages, charming women were seen in that splendid land.
43.7: Their tresses were glossy and beautiful. Their cheeks were fine and their forelocks steady. Their teeth were like the clearly \ Isible lightning streaks. Their faces were like the full moon. They bent their necks in exhibiting their emotions with gesticulation and charming twists; their ears were adorned with ornaments.
43.8: Their lips were red like Bimba fruits. They shone with their mouths coloured by chewing betal leaves. They were bedecked in golden ornaments.
43.9: Some were dark-complexioned, some were fair-comple- xioned; they had fine buttocks, their girdles and armlets produc¬ ed charming sounds-. They wore divine garlands and garments; they applied divine scents and unguents over their bodies.
43.10: The women were clever and competent. They were lovely with attractive faces and charming limbs. They were pleasing to look at. They were endowed with beauty and good colour and form. They had smiling faces.
43.11: Mad and intoxicated they sported about in assemblies and quadrangular court-yards. They delighted others by songs, instrumental music and spicy conversation.
43.12: The chiefs of harlots, experts in dancing and singing could also be found there. They were experts in the art of con¬ versation, scanning and scrutiny. They were endued with femi¬ nine charms and fine qualities.
43.13: There were others too, the women of noble families endowed with noble traits, chaste, fortunate and embellished by all good qualities.
43.14: Nandana: name of a celestial garden.
43.15: Rid of all his sins he will ride in an aerial chariot equipp¬ ed with all desirable things and go to heaven where there is the abode of lord Siva.
43.16: He will become glorious and assume a divine form. Bedecked in divine ornaments he will enjoy excellent pleasures until the dissolution of all living beings.

44.1: Administering the excellent country formerly, from that city, that king of great intellect, protected his subjects like his own bosom-born sons.
44.2: Thus endowed with riches and adorned by good qualities the king administered the excellent kingdom with his mind assured of realizing all cherished desires.
44.3: Once he pondered over this, in mind—"How shall I propitiate Visnu, the lord of all Yogas? How shall I propitiate lord who bestows worldly pleasures and salvation?"
44.4: After realising the greatest entity, the unchanging lord Vasudeva, he passed beyond all illusory knowledge. 1 Restraining his sense-organs, he became a seeker of liberation.
44.5: The Charioteer-soldiers followed him in chariots resem¬ bling aerial vehicles. They were decorated with flag-staffs and fanners. The soldiers carried weapons in their arms.
44.6: bhr&nti-jfl&na —illusory knowledge, such as the knowledge of "snake in rope or of silver in a shell". This is known as the pratibhisika jnana.
44.7: The cavalry men followed the king with horses on a par with the wind. They carried javelins and iron clubs.
44.8: There were people who sold missiles, those who sustain¬ ed themselves by trading in betal leaves, the sellers of grass, the sellers of fuel.
44.9: All those who sustained themselves by the stage, those who sold meat, oil-mongers and cloth merchants followed him.
44.10: Sellers of fruits, those who sold leaves, those who tiansported grass and fodder and thousands of washermen (followed him).
44.11: There were cowherds, barbers, tailors, shepherds, goat¬ herds and those who tended deer and swans.
44.12: There were people who sold foodgrains, powdered fried grains, gaggery and salt.
44.13: There were musicians, dancers, bards, actors, story-tellers and those who are experts in Puranas.
44.14: There were poets, versifiers, composers of poems, experts in different poems, followers of Garutfa who dispel poison and those who test different jewels.
44.15: There were blacksmiths, coppersmiths, those who work in bellmctal, Ruthakas?, those who make scabbards, painters, turners and Pavakas.
44.16: There 'were makers of sticks and batons, those who make swords, those who maintain by selling ale or gambling;
44.17: All these citizens and those who have not yet been mentioned followed him. The entire residents of the city followed him too.
44.18: Just as the sons eager to sec other villages follow their father who proceeds ahead so also those citizens followed him.
44.19: Thus the glorious king surrounded by a great concourse of people as well as (the four divisions of the army viz the ele¬ phants, horses, chariots and infantry, proceeded slowly.
44.20: Going ahead thus, followed by the armies the king reached the shore of the Southern sea after a long time.
44.21: . After reaching the sea-shore the king encamped there in a beautiful holy land endowed with the qualities of a good land.

45.4: Delicious foodstuffs of various kinds prepared with rice, sugarcane, barley milk and milk products were served to guests. The excellent king himself approached them and ordered for the immediate supply of things they wanted.

45.6: O great Boar 1 just as the earth had been formerly lifted up by you by your curved fangs, from the nether worlds so also save me from the ocean of misery.
45.7: O lord Krsna, these idols of yours, the bestowers of boons, have been eulogised by me. You, Baladeva and others, are stationed in separate forms.
45.8: This refers to the Boar incarnation of VisijLU. The boar entered the sea and found out the earth that had sunk. The boar lifted the earth at his tusks, came out of the ocean and set the earth firm over the water. On the way, the fierce and wicked Hiranyaksa hindered him. The Boar killed Hirayaksa and disappeared.
45.9: Guardians of quarters —lokapalas. They are sometimes regarded as the guardian deities of different orders of beings, but more commonly of the four cardinal and four intermediate points of the world. They are 1 Indra, of East; 2 Agni of South-east; 3 Yama of South; 4 Surya of South¬ west; 5 Varuna of West; 6 Vayu of North-west; 7 Kubera of North; 8 liana of North-east. Others substitute Nirfti for Surya and Iiani or Pfthivi for liana. According to Dharraa-saiigraha, the Buddhists enumerate 14 lokapalas.

45.16: O lord, I have passed through births, thousands and ten thousands of them of diverse kinds, in this world.
45.17: Separations from and union with wives, enemies, friends and kinsmen have been faced by me. Many and many kinds of fathers have been seen by me.
45.18: Many miseries have been experienced by me. Many miseries have been misunderstood and enjoyed as pleasures by me. I have had cousins and kinsmen, sons and brothers, in plenty.
45.19: I have lived within the belly of women that abounds in urine and floating masses of faeces. O lord, great misery has been experienced by me while staying in womb.
45.20: O lord, all those miseries that are usual in childhood, youth and old age have been suffered by me.
45.21: The miseries at death, in the path and the abode of Yama as also the tortures in hell have been experienced by me.

48.1: Paflcar&tra —a system of spiritual doctrines, by following which one attains, the position of Uparicara. O great Boar 1 just as the earth had been formerly lifted up by you by your curved fangs, from the nether worlds so also save me from the ocean of misery. O lord Krsna, these idols of yours, the bestowers of boons, have been eulogised by me. You, Baladeva and others, are stationed in separate forms.
48.2: This refers to the Boar incarnation of VisijLU. The boar entered the sea and found out the earth that had sunk. The boar lifted the earth at his tusks, came out of the ocean and set the earth firm over the water. On the way, the fierce and wicked Hiranyaksa hindered him. The Boar killed Hirayaksa and disappeared. Guardians of quarters —lokapalas. They are sometimes regarded as the guardian deities of different orders of beings, but more commonly of the four cardinal and four intermediate points of the world. They are 1 Indra, of East; 2 Agni of South-east; 3 Yama of South; 4 Surya of South¬ west; 5 Varuna of West; 6 Vayu of North-west; 7 Kubera of North; 8 liana of North-east. Others substitute Nirfti for Surya and Iiani or Pfthivi for liana. According to Dharraa-saiigraha, the Buddhists enumerate 14 lokapalas. Hara, Sankarsana and others who have been glorified as your variant forms, have been evolved for your worship. They are dependent on you, they resort to you for support.
48.3: O lord of Devas, in fact, you have no other form separate from you. The various forms of yours are only for your worship by the devotees. O lord, how can man mention you as twofold, you who are one and only one. You are all-pervading Consciousness by nature and you are unsullied. O lord of Devas, most excellent one among Devas, O bestower of freedom from fear on devotees, O deity with eyes like the petals of lotus, save me. I am immersed in the ocean of sexual objects.
48.4: Excepting you, O lord of worlds, O husband of Lak§ml, I do not see any one in whom I can seek refuge. O slayer of Madhu, 1 be pleased. O slayer of Madhu. Madhu and Kaifabha sprang from the ears of Visnu. They were about to kill Brahma who was lying on the lotus sprin¬ ging from Visnu's navel. Visnu killed them and obtained the names: Kaitabhari and Madhusudana. O lord, I have passed through births, thousands and ten thousands of them of diverse kinds, in this world.
48.5: Separations from and union with wives, enemies, friends and kinsmen have been faced by me. Many and many kinds of fathers have been seen by me. Many miseries have been experienced by me. Many miseries have been misunderstood and enjoyed as pleasures by me. I have had cousins and kinsmen, sons and brothers, in plenty. I have lived within the belly of women that abounds in urine and floating masses of faeces. O lord, great misery has been experienced by me while staying in womb.
48.6: O lord, all those miseries that are usual in childhood, youth and old age have been suffered by me. The miseries at death, in the path and the abode of Yama as also the tortures in hell have been experienced by me. O lord, many times I have been the slave of glorious prosperous men. From the impoverished state I had attained the state of a lord and master.
48.7: Many were killed by me. I have been killed by many. I have caused death to many and my death has been caused by many. Much had been given to me by others and many times gifts have been distributed by me. A fugitive (terrified of life) attacked by grief and greed I have become senseless. Now, O lord, utterly helpless and confused, I seek refuge in you.
48.8: O lord, save me who have become miserable and immersed in the ocean of worldly existence. O lord of the uni¬ verse, if you consider me your devotee have pity on me. Excepting you I have no other kinsmen who may have some consideration for me. O lord, after resorting to you, my lord, I cease to have any fear from any quarter or direction. The idea often occurs in Sanskrit poetry.
48.9: O excellent sages, the Garuda-cmblemed deity who was eulogised thus by him became pleased with him and granted him the boon of his choice. He who worships the lord of the universe every day and eulogises him by this hymn, shall become intelligent. He shall certainly obtain liberation.
48.10: The pure man who repeats this excellent hymn during the three Sandhyas every day shall attain virtue, wealth, love and liberation. He shall surely become a scholar. He who reads, listens to and narrates this with great concentration shall shake off his sins and obtain the divine world. It should not be imparted to an atheist, a fool, an un¬ grateful person, an arrogant or to one of wicked intellect. It should never be handed over to a knave.
48.11: It should be imparted to one endowed with devotion, good qualities and good conduct, to a devotee of Visnu, to a calm person habituated to perform his duty with faith. This hymn Karunyastava (a hymn of mercy) causes destruction of sins. It bestows happiness and salvation, and grants desires. This hymn of the lord mentioned by me is the most excellent of all.

49.1: At the time of going to bed his thought was—"How does Vasudeva, the lord of Devas become visible? How is that lord going to dispel my agony?
49.2: Vasudeva, the preceptor of the universe revealed himself to the sleeping king as one who held conch, discus and iron club.
49.3: O king, go there alone in a sportful mood. Take an axe
49.4: After saying this, Lord Visnu, the highly blessed deity, vanished from sight. On account of this vision in his dream the king was extremely surprised.
49.5: The king spent that night eagerly expecting (what had been foretold). His mind dwelt on it alone. He repeated the Mantras and hymns pertaining to Visnu.
49.6: Neither a chariot nor a charioteer, neither an elephant nor a foot-soldier accompanied him. The highly intelligent king entered the great shore alone.
49.7: In the course of a dream I have been directed by the lord of Devas the noblest and the greatest Soul. It has thus been narrated to you two.

50.1: The deity whom the Yogins call Vasudeva can be com¬ prehended only through perfect knowledge. It is mentioned in all scriptures. The lord is mentioned (as Brahma) in Vedanta texts.
50.2: I am Brahma, Visnu and Siva. I am Indra, the king of Devas. I am Yama who restrains the universe.
50.3: I am the earth and other elements. I am the three¬ fold sacrificial fire. 1 O king, I am also the firegod swallowing what is consigned into him. I am Varuna, lord of Waters. I am earth and the supporter of the Earth.
50.5: O excellent king of good holy rites! I am pleased with you. Choose any boon that you wish. Whatever is desired by you, whatever is cherished in the heart by you, I shall give you immediately.
50.6: Persons without merit do not have my vision even in a dream. Due to your steadfast devotion you have seen me directly.
50.7: O brahmins, on hearing these words of Vasudeva the king experienced horripilation all over his body and he recited the following prayer:
50.8: After eulogising thus, he bowed to the lord with palms joined m reverence. After bowing down and falling down on the ground he said.
50.9: May everything be to your welfare. Obtain everything desired by you. Everything will happen as you wish by my favour. There is no doubt about it.
50.10: O excellent king, rule over the great kingdom conti¬ nuously for ten thousand nine hundred years.
50.11: This sacred water-reservoir named Indradyumna- saras is born as a part of sacrifice. By taking bath in it even for once, people attain the world of Indra.
50.12: He who offers rice balls on the splendid bank of the lake shall redeem twentyone generations and go to the world of Indra.
50.13: He will go there in aerial chariot honoured by celes¬ tial damsels and the divine musicians singing in loud voice. He shall stay therefor the duration of fourteen Indras.

54.1: O excellent sages, after coming out of the belly of that boy, he once again saw the earth turned into a vast sheet of water. It was devoid of people.
54.2: He saw that same lord in the form of the infant boy whom he had seen before. He was stationed on the branch of banyan tree in a palanquin.
54.3: That lord had the scar Srlvatsa on his chest. He was clad in yellow robes and had four arms. His wide eyes resembl¬ ed the large petals of the lotus and he stayed there taking up the universe.
54.4: On seeing the sage floating and swimming like a sense¬ less person and approaching him after coming out of his mouth, the lord spoke with laugh.
54.5: O dear one, I hope you stayed in my belly comfort¬ ably and have had your rest. While wandering about what wonderful thing did you observe there?
54.6: O excellent sage, you are my devotee and have resorted completely to me. But you are tired. Hence, to help you I speak to you. See me again.
54.7: O lord of Devas, O lord of Universe, you have assumed the form of a boy by your Maya, O beautiful lotus¬ eyed one, save me, I am miserable and I have sought refuge in you.
54.8: Omost excellent one among Devas, I am scorched by the fire called Samvarta. O lord, save me. I am afraid of the rising of sparks pf fire in flames.
54.9: Scoiched by theAdityas, Pralayavartaka and others, I do not derive peace. Save me, O lord.
54.10: 1 am thirsty and afflicted by hunger. O lord of uni¬ verse, I am miserable too. I do not see any saviour. Save me, O lord.
54.11: In this terrible vast sheet of water, as the mobile and immobile beings have perished I do find no resort, save me, O lord.
54.12: O lord of Devas, the mobile and immobile beings were seen by me in your belly. I am surprised and bewildered. Save me, O lord.
54.13: In this worldly existence that has no basic support, be pleased O Lord, O most excellent one among Devas, be pleased. O deity fond of the learned and Devas, be pleased.
54.14: Be pleased, O Lord of the learned. Be pleased, O support of the learned. Be pleased, O lord of the worlds, O cause of the cause of the Universe.
54.15: Be pleased, O lord of Devas. Be pleased with me, O deity that bear the burden of the earth. Be pleased, O deity residing in waters. Be pleased, O slayer of Madhu demon.
54.16: Be pleased, O lover of Laksml, be pleased, O lord of Devas. Be pleased, O slayer of Kamsa and Kesin. Be pleased O destroyer of Arista. 1
54.17: Be pleased, O Kjrsna, O destroyer of* Daityas. Be pleased, O slayer of Danu's sons. Be pleased, O resident of Mathura. Be pleased, O scion of the family of Yadus.
54.18: Arista,: An asura, a servant of Kamsa. Once, at the instance of Kamsa he went to Gokula disguised as an ox to kill Srikrsna. The ox instilled terror in people by crushing hills and mountains, with its horns and bellowing like a bull. 54.19: You are the Purusa, the seed of the Universe. You are more excellent than others. You arc the sense-organs. O lord, you are the objects, and subtle primary elements.
54.20: You arc the guardian of the quarters. You are Devas, Yajfias and sacrificial gifts. You are Indra, Siva, offer¬ ing and the sacrificial fire.
54.21: You are Yama, the lord of manes; O lord, you are the lord of Raksasas (Nirrti) himself. You are Varuna, lord of waters; you are wind and the lord of wealth (Kubera).
54.22: You arc Isana, Ananta, Ganesa, Sanmukha, Vasus, Rudras, Adilyas and Khecaras (Planets).
54.23: You arc Isana, Ananta, Ganesa, Sanmukha, Vasus, Rudras, Adilyas and Khecaras (Planets).

55.1: Thus eulogised by Markaneya, O brahmins, the lord became pleased. He said in a voice as majestic as the rumbling sound of clouds.
55.2: O excellent sage, tell me freely what you have in your mind. O brahmanical sage, I shall give you everything, what¬ ever you may desire from me.
55.3: O lord, 1 wish to know you. O bestower of salvation, I wish to'*know your Maya (Illusion). O lord of Devas, by your favour, my power of memory is not impaired.
55.4: I have hurriedly wandered through your body. O lord, I entered your body through your mouth. O lord, I saw all worlds in your belly.
55.5: O lotus-eyed one, I wish to know you, the unchanging one.
55.6: O lotus-eyed one, I wish to hear everything in detail and in the precise manner. O lord, what I have seen is immense and inconceivable.
55.7: Thus requested by him, the lord of Devas of great refulgence, the foremost among the eloquent ones spoke the following words to Markanqleya.
55.8: Admittedly, O brahmin, Devas do not know me in reality. Out of affection for you I shall tell you how I create this universe and discharge it.
55.9: O brahminical sage, you are one with great filial affec¬ tion. You have sought refuge in me alone. Your celebacy is great. Hence, I have seen directly.
55.10: I am Narayana; I am the permanent unchanging, source of origin, the dispenser of destiny and the annihilator of all living beings.
55.11: O excellent brahmins, I am Visnu, I am Brahma, I am Indra too. T am king VaiSravana 1 and Yama the Lord of ghosts.
55.12: O excellent brahmin, I am Siva, Soma and patriarch Kasyapa. I am creator and dispenser of destiny and I am sacrifice too.
55.14: Badava: the fire of sage Aurva's penance which started to burn the world but which, at the request of pitrs he threw down into the sea where it took the shape of a horse-head and living beneath the sea continued vomiting heat at all times.
55.15: Thus, O excellent sage, for the duration of the period till Brahma rises up I remain in the form of an infant though. I am not an infant.
55.16: O leading brahmin, honoured and worshipped by brahminical sages, boon has been granted to you by. me in the form of Brahma. I have been propitiated many times.
55.17: When the mobile and immobile beings had perished you set out. Seeing everything in a vast sheet of water you were bewildered. It was observed by me and hence you were shown the universe.
55.18: O brahmins, after saying this, when the period of a thousand sets of four Yugas was completed the lord again spoke to him in a voice as majestic as the sound of rumbling cloud.

56.1: O brahmins, henceforth, I shall recount the mode of visiting the five Tlrthas (holy centres) and the benefit derived from holy dips,.charitable gifts and visits to the deities.
56.2: The pure man should go to the eddy called Markandeya Hrada and dive therein facing the north. He should take the holy dips thrice and repeat this Mantra,
56.3: After taking the holy dip in the water of depth upto the umbilicus, the intelligent devotee should duly perform Tarpana of Devas, sages, manes, and others by means of water mixed with gingelly seeds.
56.4: By taking the holy dip in the eddy of Markanqleya Hrada, thus, and by visiting Sankara, the man obtains the benefit of ten horse-sacrifices.
56.5: Thereafter, the devotee should go to the holy fig tree on a par with the Kalpa tree, circumambulate it thrice and worship the banyan tree with great devotion, repeating the following Mantra:—
56.6: By devoutly circumambulating and bowing down to the Banyan tree resembling the Kalpa tree the man is imme¬ diately liberated from sins like the serpent that is rid of its old and decaying slough.
56.7: O brahmins, even by passing through the shadow of this Kalpa tree, a man eschews the sin of brahmin slaughter. What doubt is there in regard to other sins?
56.8: By making obeisance to Vainateya, Garuda son of Vinata who is stationed in front of Krsna, the devotee shall be¬ come, liberated from all sins. He shall then go to the city of Visnu.
56.9: He who visits Purusottama, Samkarsana and Su- bhadra after visiting the banyan tree and Vainateya, attains the greatest goal.
56.10: After entering the shrine of Visnu and circumambu¬ lating the lord thrice he should worship and propitiate San- karsana and Subliadra, repeating their own Mantra:—
56.11: After worshipping the ploughshare-bearing lord thus, the clever devotee shall worship Krsna with great concentra¬ tion uttering the twelve-syllabled Mantra.
56.12: The self-possessed bold persons who devoutly worship Purusottama by reciting the twelve-syllabled Mantra attain Salvation.
56.13: O brahmins, neither Devas nor Yogins, nor the Chanters of Saman hymns attain that goal which those who are devoted to the twelve-syllabled Mantra attain.
56.14: Hence, one should devoutly worship Krsna, the pre¬ ceptor of the universe, by reciting that Mantra alone. After worshipping with scents, fragrant flowers, etc. he should bow to the deity and propitiate him.
56.15: By visiting and bowing to Krsna the man obtains that benefit which has been glorified as the result of holy dip and charitable gifts in the holy centres.
56.16: By visiting and bowing to Krsna a man obtains that benefit which results from a sacrifice where much gold is distri¬ buted together with precious stones and other valuables.
56.17: By making obeisance to Krsna a man obtains that benefit which has been glorified as the result of sacrifices and the Vedas.
56.18: By visiting and bowing to Krsna a man obtains that benefit which is attained by all charitable gifts, holy rites and observances.

57.1: By thus visiting and bowing to Bala, Krsna and Su- bhadra, the devotee obtains virtue, wealth, love and liberation.
57.2: He returns to his abode where lord Visnu's idol, made of lapis lazuli, is covered up by sands. By bowing to the lord who vanished there he enters the city of Visnu.
57.3: By devoutly visiting Narasimha lord, and by bowing to him one is liberated from all sins. There is no doubt in this.
57.4: Hence, by all means one shall resort to Narasimha since he bestows the benefit of virtue, wealth, love and salvation.
57.5: O lord of the universe, we wish to hear the power of that lord in detail. Our eagerness is very great.
57.6: O lord, obeisance be to you. For rendering help to devotees, tell us how Narasimha, the lord of great strength becomes pleased.
57.7: We hear many human and divine accomplishments which are undoubtedly realized by the favour of that lord.
57.8: Due to the favour of that lord, one's movement be¬ comes unimpeded in the mortal world, heaven, netherworlds, quarters, water, city as well as mountain.
57.9: In this world including the mobile and immobile beings O brahmins, there is nothing impossible to achieve for lord Narasimha who is always sympathetic to his devotees.
57.10: I shall mention the mode of procedure for the worship of the lord. This is helpful to his devotees. I shall mention what it is whereby the deity with half the body of a lion is propitiated.
57.11: O leading sages, listen to the eternal Kalparaja (Royal ritual), the real principle of Narasimha which has not been understood by Devas and Asuras.
57.12: O brahmins, the leading aspirant devotee should subsist on a diet of milk accompanied by greens, roots, barley food, fruits, fried grain powder and oil cake.
57.13: It should also protect from all those enemies such as Gandharvas, Kinnaras, Yaksas, Vidyadharas, Nagas, goblins, demons as well as similar antagonists.
57.14: The learned aspirant shall unhesitatingly enter the Crevasse with the coat of mail on, as he goes ahead, his diffi¬ culty, darkness and delusion perish.
57.15: A wide royal road beautified by humming bees becomes visible. O brahmins, remembering Narasimha he enters the nether worlds.
57.16: The amulet (inspired with Narasimha Mantra)' tied round the neck of children affords a permanent protection: It destroys tumour, pustule, boils, as well as spider poison.
57.17: If afflicted by ailments, the devotee should perform a sacrifice with sacrificial twigs, ghee and milk, thrice a day during the junctions (i.e. dawn, midday and dusk). If this is continued for a month it will dispel all ailments.
57.18: Hence, O leading sages, the devotee should always worship the lord of beasts, of great power, the bestower of all desires.

58.3: In his kingdom, men used to live upto ten thousand years without sickness. No body perished or was despondant in that kingdom.

58.7: O Lord of Devas, O Lord of the Universe, O unchang¬ ing source of origin of the three worlds, tell us now the greatest fact of the deity named Sveta.

59.1: He goes to the greatest abode where Hari himself is present. Returning to this placc(eartli)in due course of time he shall become a king on the earth,
59.2: By resorting to Matsyamadhava a man becomes un- thwartable. He shall be a donor, enjoyer of pleasures, a wor¬ shipper, a devotee of Visnu and truthful in speech.
59.3: Afterwards he attains Yoga pertaining to Hari and gains salvation. O leading sages, the greatness of Matsyama¬ dhava has been recounted by me. By visiting him the devotee will obtain all cherished desires.

59.5: The Pancatlrthi (a set of five holy centres and sacred waters) is as follows:—The eddy named after Markandeya, the holy banyan tree, the shrine of Kfsna, the shrine of Bala- rama and the great Indradyumnasaras (Lake of Indra- dyumna).
59.6: One should visit the Tlrtfiaraja (king of holy centres, the holy Banyan tree) on the full moon day in the month of Jyestha. If the constellation Jyestha coincides with it, it is especially auspicious.
59.7: O brahmins, I shall mention its names and size, in the Yugas Krta, etc, in due order.
59.8: The names of the banyan tree in the Kjtayuga etc are respectively.—1) Vata, (2). Vatesvara, (3) Purusa and (4) Puranapurusa, O brahmins.
59.9: The sizes of the Kalpa tree in the four Yugas are 1) one Yojana 2) three fourths of a Yojana (3) half a Yojana and 4) onefourth of a Yojana.
59.10: After bowing to the banyan tree repeating the mantra mentioned before, the devotee shall go to the South to a distance of three hundred bow's lengths.
59.11: By bowing to him and then by worshipping him, the devotee is liberated from all ailments, sins, evils and things of other sorts.
59.12: The waters are glorified as Naras because they are the sons ofNara (human beings). At the outset the waters had been the abode of Visnu. Hence, he is known as Narayana (having Nara (waters) for abode.
59.13: Particularly at the time of bath the pure devotee shall worship and remember Narayana in the water. He shall meditate on him and perform the Nyasa rite in the (fingers of hand and (the limbs of) body.
59.14: I am lord Narayana who holds the conch, discus and club. After meditating on the Self he should repeat this mantra.
59.15: After performing the rites of ablution and cleansing by means of the Mantras with the water as their divinity, the devotee shall thereafter repeat the Aghamarsana Mantra three times (all the while) standing within water.
59.16: O brahmins, just as the horse-sacrifice removes sins so also does the hymn Aghamarsana 1 remove all sins.
59.17: After circumambulating the sungod and bowing down to him he should sit facing the east and perform the rite of (ve ic study, then he should perform Tarpana rites to the Gods and sages.
59.18: He s hould perform Tarpana rites for sages, manes and ot lers. He the knower of Mantras, should perform Tarpana
59.20: The brahmin shall be authorized in the Tarpana rite
59.21: At the time ofSraddha, when the ball office is offered, the devotee shall offer it with a single hand. When performing the rite of Tarpana he shall use both hands. This is the pro¬ cedure to be followed always.
59.22: After repeating the name and Gotra (Spiritual line¬ age) he shall say 'Trpyatam' (may be pleased). Otherwise he should not utter anything. The left-hand should be joined to the right hand (and thus the libation should be offered.
59.23: If out of delusion the devotee performs the rite of Tar¬ pana with the gingclly seeds kept on any of his limbs, it would be as though he had performed the rites of Tarpana to the forefathers by means of skin, flesh, blood and bone.
59.24: One should notperform the rite of Tarpana to the deities and Pitrs with the gingclly seeds kept on any of the limbs. That water will turn into blood and he who offers it shall be sinful.

59.26: If the man stands on the ground and offers libation into the water, that water libation does not approach the manes. It turns futile.

60.1: After drawing the mystic diagram O brahmins, the devotee should worship Narayana, the unborn lord by means of injunctions in regard to the eight syllabled Mantra.
60.2: Then he should perform the Nyasa rite with the eight- syllabled Mantra. He shall begin with the left foot and fix in due order.
60.3: The aspirant should perform the following rites with the basic Mantra viz. the five limbs belonging to lord Visnu;
60.4: Om obeisance to Visnu—thus the head. Om obeisance tojvalana (the fiery blaze)—thus the tuft. Om obeisance to Visnu—thus the coat of mail. Om obeisance to Visnu—thus the throbbing for the binding of quarters. Om Hum phat—thus the miraculous weapon. Om Vasudeva is white—in the head thus. Om Am Sarikarsana is red—in the forehead. Garuda is the fire, the luminary sun thus. Aril Pradyumna is yellow—in the neck. He is the wind and cloud. Orh ArhAniruddha is black—in the heart. He is endowed with all power. Thus protected by four arrays the devotee shall start reciting Kavaca.
60.5: He should perform the worship of eternal lord by the twelve-syllabled Mantra; thereafter he should fix it up in the pericarp, at the outside, after retaining it in the heart.
60.6: He should meditate upon the eternal lord with four arms and possessed of great strength. He should think upon the lord with lustre of a crore suns. He should invoke the lord after duly thinking about him in his mind.
60.8: Om the water offering for washing the wet. O Eternal Padmanabha, O Lord, the water is offered at your feet. O Visnu, with eyes like the petals of a lotus, O Madhusudana, please accept it. Om namo Narayanaya (Obeisance to Narayana)—thus the Padya.
60.9: Madhuparka: a mixture ofhoney, curd and butter offered to the guest or the bridegroom on the wedding ceremony.

62.2: The intelligent devotee should go there with pure mind and body, and meditate mentally on lord Hari, approach the sacred waters, perform the Acamana rite and repeat this Mantra:—
62.3: "O holy spot that is sanctified by the performance of horse sacrifice, and which destroys sins, I am taking a holy dip in you. Remove my sin. Obeisance be to you".
62.4: He redeems seven former generations and seven sub¬ sequent generations of his family. Like a God he goes to the world of Visnu on an aerial chariot that can go in all directions.
62.5: He can enjoy pleasures and happiness there, as long as the moon, sun and stars last. Falling off* from that world he returns to the earth and attains salvation thereafter.
62.6: O lord, great-grandfather, why do you praise the month of Jyestha in preference to Magha and other months. Kindly tell us the reason thereof.
62.7: O leading sages, listen, I shall briefly mention why I praise the month of Jyestha. in preference to other months.
62.8: O excellent brahmins, the tenth day in the bright half of the month of Jyestha removes ten sins. Hence it is called 'Dasahara'.
62.9: The man who visits Balarama, Krsna, and Subhadra meditates upon them with concentration and mental purity will get rid of all sins and go to the world of Visnu.

66.1: Mention separately the benefit which a man or a woman with perfect self-control acquires by making holy pilgrimage.
66.2: O brahmins, even as I recount, listen to the benefit of holy pilgrimage severally, that a man acquires after under¬ taking the pilgrimage to that holy centre with great restraint.
66.3: A man undoubtedly enjoys pleasures for as many Kalpas as the number of times he undertakes pilgrimages in the month of Jyestha.
66.4: O Lord, we wish to hear, even as you recount, the installation and worship of the lord of the universe and the mode of these rites as well as charitable gifts and the fruits thereof. O leading sages, listen to the installation of idols urged by Brahma. By devoutly performing this, the man or the woman acquires the benefit.
66.5: O excellent brahmins, when the twelve pilgrimages are completed, the devotee should carry out the installation that destroy sin.
66.6: The rite of holy bath should be performed in accord¬ ance with the injunctions prescribed by the sages in regard to him. After taking holy bath perfectly in accordance with the injunction (the devotee) who is conversant with the names, Gotras (spiritual lines) and the procedure, should perform Tarpana rite to Devas, sages and manes as well as others.
66.7: He should repeat other holy passages and Mantras pertaining to the sun with faith and concentration. After making three circumambulations he should bow down to the Sungod.
66.8: In regard to the people of the first three castes the rite of holy bath and the repetition of Mantras is in the manner mentioned in the Vedas. The utterance of the Vedic passage is to be avoided by women as well as Sudras. With great devotion he shall worship Lord Visnu offering lotuses and other flowers pertaining to Visnu (like jasmine etc.).
66.9: After worshipping the lord the ruler of the universe, the bestower of worldly pleasures and salvation, in this manner, he shall burn incense along with agallochum in front of the lord.
66.10: O excellent sages, he shall burn aromatic resin too along with scents. He shall light a lamp with devotion using ghee (instead of oil) according to the means. With concentration he shall offer twelve other lamps, O excellent sages, he shall burn it with ghee or gingelly oil.
66.11: By way of Naivedya (food offering) he shall dedicate milk pudding, sweet Saskulis, Vatakas (special kinds of baked or fried cakes) sweets, a little quantity of molasses and fruits too.
66.12: After worshipping Purusottama with five items of service (i.e. bathing, offering cloths, worshipping with flowers, showing lamps and incense and food offerings) the devotee shall repeat "Om obeisance to Purusottama" a hundred and eight times. With faith and concentration, O excellent sages, the devotee shall make a flowery bowerlike Mantfapa over the lord.
66.13: Thereafter, he shall resolve to keep awake at night. For this purpose he shall arrange for the discourses on the divine story of Vasudeva or devotional songs.
66.14: After taking bath perfectly in accordance with the in¬ junctions, the devotee shall control his sense organs and put on washed (and dried) clothes. Thereafter, he shall bathe lord Visnu with devotion as before. Thereafter, he should give the preceptor a cow, cloth, gold, umbrella, pair of sandals, foodgrain and bellmetal vessel with devotion.
66.15: He should feed brahmins. The food served should begin with milk pudding. There should be sweet cooked rice and various kinds of edibles prepared in jaggery and ghee.
66.16: After the brahmins have been fed to their satisfaction and their minds are at rest, he should give them twelve water pots together with sweets. Devoid of revelry he should give them monetary gifts according to his capacity.
66.17: O excellent brahmins, after worshipping those brah¬ mins, he should devotedly worship his preceptor who is the bestower of perfect knowledge and who is on a par with Visnu
66.18: The learned devotee should honour him with gold cloth, cow, foodgrains and other articles. Thereafter, he should repeat this mantra. "May Lord Purusottama who has neither beginning nor end, who holds conch, discus and iron club and who is the omnipresent lord of the Universe be pleased with this.
66.19: After uttering this mantra he should circumambulate brahmins thrice. He should bid farewell to the preceptor by bending his head with devotion.
66.20: Thereafter, he should follow those brahmins with devo¬ tion to the boundary of the village. Thus following them he should pay homage and bid them farewell. Accompanied by kinsmen and relatives he should take
66.21: By performing this rite perfectly well, the devotee whether a man or a woman should derive the benefit of thou¬ sands of horse-sacrifices and a hundred Rajasuya sacrifices.
66.22: For a period of thirty Kalpas he enjoys excellent plea¬ sures there as he wishes. From there, O excellent brahmins he comes to the world of the moon. O excellent brahmins, after enjoying splendid pleasures there for a period of ten Kalpas he comes to the world of Gan- dharvas which is most difficult of access.
66.23: After enjoying various pleasures to the fullest satisfac¬ tion for the period of a Kalpa, he comes to the earth and be¬ comes a virtuous king.

68.1: O excellent sages, the truth, the very truth has been cited by us on all. There is no other holy centre on Earth that is equal to Purusottama.
68.2: All those holy centres and shrines do not deserve even a sixteenth part of Purusottama.
68.3: Just as Visnu has been cited as the most excellent one among the sons of Aditi so also Purusottama is the most ex¬ cellent one among the holy centres.
68.4: Just as the moon among the stars and ocean among lakes so also the holy centre of Purusottama is the most excellent among the holy centres.
68.5: Like (fire).among the Vasus and Sankara among the Rudras, so also Purusottama is the most excellent of all holy centres.
68.6: Like brahmins among the four castes and Garuda among the birds, Purusottama is the most excellent of all holy centres.
68.7: Like LaksmI among young women and Gariga among the rivers Purusottama is the most excellent of all holy centres.
68.8: Like Uccaissravas among the horses, like Usanas among the poets, Purusottama is the most excellent of all holy centres.

69.1: We are not satiated by listening to the story of the lord. It behoves you to relate once again the great secret doctrine.
69.2: . The details of Vasudeva the infinite deity have not been explained perfectly by you. O lord, wc wish to hear. Kindly mention it in detail.
69.3: O excellent sages, I shall mention the greatest essence, the greatness of the infinite deity Vasudeva, the rarest in the three worlds.
69.4: Formerly, in the Adikalpa (first of the Kalpas), O brahmins, I was born of the unmanifest. Visvakarman spoke these words.
69.5: The glorious and righteous Vibhlsana, the younger brother and minister of Ravana was a devotee of Narayana. He was entrusted with the administration of the capital Lanka.
69.6: O king, it behoves you to favour me with this idol. O lord of the worlds, I shall propitiate it irnd cross the ocean of worldly existence.
69.7: Those who devoutly resort to the infinite lord of all, mentally, verbally and physically attain the highest region.
69.8: By visiting Ananta (infinite) even for once and by devoutly worshipping and bowing to him, the devotee derives ten.times more than the benefit of Rajasuya and Asvamedha sacrifices.

70.1: Thus, the glory of (Infinite deity) and the holy shrine of Purusottama that yields worldly pleasures and liberation unto men has been recounted by me. It is very difficult of access.
70.2: KtSin: a follower of Kaiiisa who at the instruction of Kamsa went to Gokula, in the form of a horse, to kill Srikrs*a. But Snkrsna killed him and got the name Kesava.
70.3: Those who meditate upon Krsna the overlord of the three worlds', the bestower of all desired benefits, are liberated souls.
70.4: Those who are devoted to Krsna, those who remember Krsna at night (when they go to bed) and again when they get up enter Krsna when their bodies are consumed on death like the ghee offering consigned to fire with due repetitions of Mantras.
70.5: Hence, O excellent sages, the lotus-eyed deity Krsna should be assiduously visited in that holy centre by those who seek salvation.
70.6: The lofty-minded persons who visit Krsna, (Balarama) and Subhadra at the time when the deities are laid to rest go to the world of Visnu.
70.7: Those who devoutly visit Purusottama, Balarama and Subhadra at any time, go to the world of Visnu.
70.8: He who stays in the holy centres of Purusottama for the four months of rainy season derives more benefit than the benefit accruing from the holy pilgrimage to the other centres of the Earth.
70.9: Those lofty persons who reside there itself during the seasons, after conquering sense-organs and controlling anger, derive the benefit of a penance.
70.10: Within a month a man obtains at Purusottama their benefit which others obtain after performing penance in other holy centres for ten thousand years.
70.11: Everyday, the pure person derives that benefit which is mentioned as the result of perfectly performed pilgrimage, holy rites and observances.
70.12: A man of perfectly restrained sense-organs obtains everyday the same benefit as one obtains (on other holy centres) after performing different rites of sacrifice.
70.13: Those who abandon their bodies anywhere between the baniyan tree and the Ocean obtain* the greatest liberation which is very difficult to get.
70.14: Even the animals of low strata of species such as germs, worms, moths etc., attain the greatest salvation by abandon¬ ing their bodies there.
70.15: O brahmins, see the illusion of the world in regard to other holy centres. The fruits of all other holy centres are derived from the only holy centre Purusottama.
70.16: The man who faithfully visits Purusottama for once will become the most excellent man among thousands of men.
70.17: Hence, O excellent brahmins, one who gives up his body in this holy centre will achieve liberation.
70.18: Who can adequately mention the glory of Puru¬ sottama? Just by visiting the baniyan tree there a man dispels the sin of brahmin slaughter.

71.1: O leading sages, listen to his interesting story. I shall mention in brief the activities of that sage. During the summer he practised fivefold penance with four fires on the four sides and the sun overhead; during the rainy season he slept on the bare ground; during winter he stood in neck-deep water—thus he performed a great penance.
71.2: On seeing the power of penance of that sage, Devas, Gandharvas, Siddhas and Vidyadharas were struck with wonder. O excellent sages, with the force of his strength Kandu scorched the three worlds, Earth, firmament and heaven. On seeing him engaged in penance Devas said thus:— cc Wonderful is his great courage! Wonderful is his great penance!'
71.3: Without excitement they consulted one another. Inclu¬ ding Indra they were bewildered and frightened. Hence, they wanted an obstacle to be putin the way of his penance. O Pramloca, go quickly to the place where this sage is performing penance. O splendid lady, in order to impede his penance make his mind agitated.
71.4: O most excellent Deva, O my lord, I always carry out your behests. But in this matter, I have some doubts. My lif e has to be risked. When he comes to know that I have approached him to create impediment in his penance, sage Kandu of excessive splendour will curse me angrily. It will be unbearable. On hearing her words the consort of SacI said again;— Let others stay by. O splendid lady, you are very clever in this affair.
71.5: O lady of fine buttocks, I shall send Kama, Vasanta (Spring) and the gentle breeze to assist you. Go with them to the place where this great sage lives. On hearing the words of Indra that excellent lady of attractive eyes went with them by the aerial path.
71.6: After going there she saw the excellent and charming forest. She saw the pious sage, seated in the hermitage perform¬ ing his brilliant penance. Along with them, she surveyed the beautiful forest comparable to the Nandana forest. It contained excellent flowers of all seasons. It was agitated by groups of monkeys. Standing on the banks of the river, only a very short distance from him, that excellqnt celestial damsel with the sweetness of the cuckoo in her voice began to sing songs merrily.
71.7: An untimely but sweet and charming note of the cuckoo was heard and Vasanta exerted his full force. A gentle breeze withhis abode in the Malaya mountain blew there making the excellent flowers fall down gently into small or big heaps.
71.8: Holding the flowery arrows, Kama went near that sage and made his mind agitated. On hearing the sweet sound of the song the sage was surprised and his mind was afflicted by the arrows of Kama. He went to the place where the lady of beautiful eyebrows was standing. O lady of good buttocks, who are you? Whom do you belong to? O fortunate blessed lady of atrractive smiles, you have captivated my mind. O lady of fine eyebrows and slender waist, tell me the truth.
71.9: I have come here to collect flowers. I am your servant- maid. Command me quickly? What shall I do at your bidding? On hearing her words the sage lost his courage. He

71.14: When urged by her thus, the sage said to that lady of large eyes—"O lady of beautiful eyebrows, stay with me for a long time more: you will go later to heaven." Frightened of being cursed by that sage, the lady of fine buttocks stayed with him for a further period of slightly less than two hundred years. Once the sage went out of his hut in a great hurry. As he rushed out the splendid lady said—"Pray, where do you go?' 5
71.16: When asked by her thus he said— cc O auspicious lady, the day is coming to a close. I shall say my prayers for the dusk. Otherwise, it will be a great omission of my holy rites." The delighted lady then laughed and said to the sage— "is it only now; O sage conversant with all holy rites, that the day is coming to a close? Has it not passed of many times before?" "O brahmin, this is true that I came here in a morning. It is not false. But hundreds of years have passed by, since I came to you."
71.17: Thereupon, the brahmin asked the lady of large eyes in great perturbation—"O timid lady, even as I was engaged in dalliance with you, what period of time did pass by?" "Nine hundred, seven years, six months and three days have passed ofF till date."
71.18: "O timid lady, arc you telling me the truth or are you jesting with me? I think I have stayed here with you only for a day." "O brahmin, how will I utter a lie in your presence? Particularly when asked by you as you proceed ahead along your path?" O excellent brahmins, on hearing her words thatsage censured himself saying—"Fie upon me who have not adhered to disciplined good conduct.
71.19: After censuring himself thus, that sage conversant with piety spoke these words to tlxat celestial damsel who was seated there. O sinful lady, go away as you please. The task of the king of Dcvas has been duly accomplished by you by causing perturbation in me through your amorous gestures.
71.20: Wastage of my austerities has been brought about by you who seek the favour of Indra. Fie upon you the despicable one, the cause of great delusion. When that brahminical sage said this to that lady of fine waist, she trembled excessively and perspired profusely. Rebuked by him she went out of his hermitage and traversing the path of firmament she mopped off her sweat drops by the sprouts of trees.

73.17: Thereupon, the brahmin asked the lady of large eyes in great perturbation—"O timid lady, even as I was engaged in dalliance with you, what period of time did pass by?"
73.18: "Nine hundred, seven years, six months and three days have passed ofF till date."
73.19: "O timid lady, arc you telling me the truth or are you jesting with me? I think I have stayed here with you only for a day."
73.20: "O brahmin, how will I utter a lie in your presence? Particularly when asked by you as you proceed ahead along your path?"

74.1: Listen, O leading sages, I shall recount to you briefly the incarnations which Hari took up in order to remove the burden of the Earth.
74.2: Now, Daityas, the followers of Kalanemi have come to the mortal world. Day and night they harass the subjects.
74.3: • That Asura Kalancmi who was slain by all powerful Visnu is now born as Karhsa the great Asura and a son of Ugrasena.
74.4: On hearing these words of the Earth Brahma was requested by Devas to remove the burden of the Earth.
74.5: After saying thus Brahma went along with Devas. With full concentration, he eulogised the Garua-emblemed deity.
74.6: O lord with thousand forms, obeisance, obeisance be to you; O thousand-armed one, O many-armed and many- footcd one, obeisance, obeisance to you, O lord engaged in creation, maintenance and destruction of the universe, O incomprehensible one.
74.7: You are the subtlest of all subtle beings; you have a great magnitude, O lord, you are weightier than the weightiest. O lord, possessed of Pradhana, cosmic intellect and sense- organs, O lord identical with the chief worlds, be pleased.
74.8: On account of the mighty Asuras born on the Earth, O lord, this Earth is extremely afflicted. She is pained under the heavy weight of suffering. In order to get the burden re¬ moved she has approached you the ultimate resort of worlds, the redeemer without any other greater being.
74.9: May all Devas incarnate on the Earth. Let them fight with the mighty proud Asuras who are already born before.
74.10: O immortal ones, this hair of mine will be born as the eighth child in the womb of DevakI, the wife of Vasudeva who is comparable to a goddess.
74.12: After birth on the Earth it will kill Kamsa bom of Kalancmi. AJter saying this, Hari vanished there itself.
74.13: Those Devas then bowed down to the noble lord who became invisible, went to the top of Meru and then descended on the Earth.
74.14: The holy sage Narada said thus to Kamsa—"The eighth child in the womb of DevakI born in the Earth will kill you".
74.15: On hearing it from Narada, Kamsa became infuriated. He kept DevakI and Vasudeva as prisoners in their own house and guarded them well.
74.16: The sons of Hiranyakasipu became well known as these six children in the womb. Urged by Visnu, his (Yogic) slumber joined them gradually to the womb of DevakI.
74.17: O slumber, go hence. One by one take these children (of Hiranyakasipu) who are in the nether worlds now to the belly of DevakI at my behest.
74.18: When they have been killed by Kamsa, my sinless part named Sesa will become the seventh child in the womb of DevakI by means of a small part.
74.19: Since the child in the womb has been dragged away, the heroic boy comparable to the peak of Meru, Sankarsana will be born in the world.
74.20: Then, I shall be born in the auspicious womb of DevakI. You should also go to the womb of Yasoda without delay.
74.21: I shall be born at night on the eighth day in the dark half of the mouth of Sravana during the rainy season. You will be born on the ninth day.
74.22: O uncensured lady, urged by my Sakti, Vasudeva will take me to the bed ofYasoda and you to that of Devaki.
74.23: O gentle lady, Kamsa will seize you and hurl you against a rocky slab. Thereafter, you will attain an abode in the firmament.
74.24: With due deference to me, Indra will bow down to you a hundred times; with his head bent down in obeisance he will accept you as his sister.
74.25: Thereafter, you will kill thousands of Daityas. With various abodes (i.e. shrines) you will adorn the entire Earth.
74.26: You are identical with the following deities:—Bhuti (Existence), Sannati (Obeisance), Klrti (Renown), Kanti (Splendour), PrthivI (Earth), Dhrti (Courage), Lajja (Bashfulness), Pu?ti (Nourishment), Uma and other goddesses whoever they may be.
74.27: Worshipped by means of wine, meat and other pre¬ sents and various items of foodstuffs you will become de¬ lighted and fulfil all desires of men.
74.28: Undoubtedly, all of them will have welfare always due to my favour. It need not be suspected at all. O gentle lady, go, in the manner mentioned before.

75.1: On the same day the Yogic slumber took birth in the belly of Yasoda in accordance with what was mentioned by Brahma.
75.2: O brahmins, when the part of Visnu entered the Earth the seasons became auspicious. The planets in the sky moved perfectly (and favourably).
75.3: No one dared to look at Devaki due to her excessive refulgence. On seeing her blazing splendidly, the minds of onlookers became excited.
75.4: Day and night the deities eulogised Devaki who held Visnu in her womb.
75.5: You are Svaha, you are Svadha, you are Vidya, you are Sudha (Nectar), you are splendour. For the protection of worlds, you have incarnated on the Earth.
75.6: Thus eulogised by Devas, she conceived the lord in her womb, the lotus-eyed lord, the cause of safety and security of the world.
75.7: When at midnight, Janardana the support of all, was
75.8: May that lord ofDevas be pleased, the lord of Devas who has now revealed an infant's form by means of his own Maya, whose form is endless, whose form is this entire universe and who bears the world in his womb.
75.9: O lord, the Atman of ail, withdraw this four-armed form. O destroyer of Asuras, sons of Diti, let not Karhsa know about your incarnation.
75.10: Formerly, O gentle lady, I had been eulogised by you, desirous of a son. Since I am now born of your womb, your prayer has become fruitful.
75.11: O excellent sages, after saying thus, the lord became silent. During the night itself Vasudeva took him and went out.
75.12: When Vasudeva set out, the watchmen became deluded. The porters and watchmen of the city of Mathura were enchanted and deluded by the Yogic slumber.

75.15: On the bank of Yamuna he saw Nanda and other elderly cowherds who carried revenue to be paid to Karhsa.
75.16: On waking up, Yasoda saw her new-born son, dark in complexion like the petals of a blue lotus. Thereat she re¬ joiced very much.
75.17: Taking the baby girl back to his abode, Vasudeva placed her on the bed of Devakl.

79.1: He went to the river Kalindl that had gently moving ripples and waves and that appeared to be smiling all round by the clusters of foams sticking to the banks.
79.2: There he saw a hideous and extremely terrible whirl¬ pool of serpent Kaliya, which had been defiled by sparks of poisonous fire.
79.3: As the fire of poison spread, the great trees that grew on its banks were burnt. Even the birds (that flew over it) had been burnt when they came into contact with its watery spray as the wind wafted it up.
79.4: On seeing that highly terrible serpent which was like another jaw of Death lord Krsna thought thus:
79.5: Therefore, I shall climb this great tree of Kadamba which is not very far off from it, I shall jump into the eddy of the serpent that causes destruction.
79.6: Those trees that were sprinkled with the hot water heated by the flames of the defiled person of the serpent blazed suddenly. The flames then spread over all the quarters.
79.7: Lord Krsna clapped and dashed against the whirlpool with his arms. On hearing that sound the king of serpents approached him.
79.8: His eyes turned red due to wrath; his hoods became agitated through poisonous flames. He was surrounded by pink-coloured serpents of great poison.
79.9: There were hundreds of wives of the serpent. They appeared splendid by their attractive necklaces. Their earrings sparkled as they moved along with their jerking trembling bodies.
79.10: On seeing him fallen there afflicted by the bodies of serpents, the cowherd lads went back to Vraja (the colony of cowherds) and lamented in their excessive grief.
79.11: In his. delusion Krsna went into the eddy of Kaliya. He has sunk into it. He is being bitten by the king of serpents. Hence, all of you come. Do not delay.
79.12: On hearing these words comparable to the stunning blow of the thunderbolt, the cowherds and the cowherdesses, Yosoda and others, hastened to the eddy.
79.13: Rama of wonderful exploits, Nandagopa and other cowherds hastened to Yamuna, desirous of seeing Krsna.
79.14: O excellent sages, staring anxiously at the face of his son, Nandagopa stood motionless. The highly blessed Yosoda was also like that.
79.15: The cowherdesses and others looked on helplessly. In their extreme distress and grief they wept continuously owing to their love for Kcs'ava. Those ladies said in the frightened timidity of their minds: Ail of us shall now enter this great eddy of the king of serpents alongwith Yasoda. It is not proper on our part to go back to our colony.
79.17: He saw Nanda extremely distressed with his eyes fixed to his face. He saw Yasoda perturbed and faintingwithout being fully aware of his greatness. With both of his hands he made the middle hood bend down. As the head of the serpent king became bent he rode and danced on it.
79.18: The hood of the serpent became wounded due to the kicks from the feet of Kr§na whenever the hood was raised. After the kick his head bent low.
79.19: By frequent hits and blows from Krsna the serpent became unconscious and deluded. Due to the fierce kickings he vomited blood. On seeing that serpent had been compelled to bend his head and neck to shed blood from his mouth the wives of the serpent lord sought shelter in Krsna.
79.20: O serpent, you must not stay any longer in the waters of Yamuna, go to the waters of the ocean along with your sons and attendants.
79.21: O serpent, when he sees the imprints of my feet on your head during your stay in the ocean, Garuqla the enemy of serpents will not strike you. After saying this lordHari released the king of serpents. The serpent lord bowed down to Krsna and went to the ocean.
79.22: Even as all the living beings stood watching, the serpent king abandoned his white eddy and went away along with servants, children and kinsmen accompanied by all his wives.

80.1: Once again, Bala and Keava started tending the cows together. Wandering along the forest they came to the beautiful grove of palmyre trees.
80.2: The Asura Dhenuka occupied that palmyra grove after assuming the form of a donkey. Human flesh and beef consti¬ tuted his diet.
80.3: On seeing the beautiful palm grove richlyendowed with plenty of fruits, the cowherds became desirous of plucking those fruits. They said thus:
80.4: On hearing these words of the cowherd lads, Sariikar- sana and Krsna knocked clown the palm fruits to the ground.
80.5: On hearing the sound of the falling palmyra fruits the evil-minded king of Asuras, a son of Diti who had assumed the form of a donkey came there in great fury.
80.6: As he fell down from the top of the palm tree the dead donkey brought with him many fruits on the Earth like a gust of wind bringing down clouds.

80.8: O brahmins, thereafter without any obstruction the cows comfortably grazed fresh shoots of grass inthatpalmgrove where they had not been grazing before.
