80.10: Jesting and shouting, singing and collecting the fruits of the trees those two noble boys shone splendidly like two bulls with tiny horns.

81.1: Even as Rama and Kesava sported about thus, the rainy season passed off and the season of Autumn set in when lotuses blossomed forth.
81.2: On seeing the cowherds enthusiastic and desirous of celebrating the festival the highly intelligent Krsna spoke to the elders out of curiosity.
81.3: "What is this festival of Indra wherein you are so very delighted?"
81.4: Plants and foodgrains are produced by that rain. We and other embodied beings sustain ourselves by eating them. So we propitiate the Deities.
81.5: The land without plants and grass and people afflicted by hunger are not seen in the places where rain-bearing clouds are seen.
81.6: The cloud squeezes the terrestrial water through the rays of the sun. Parjanya, lord of the cloud, showers it on the Earth for Existence and growth of the world.
81.7: Hence, during the rainy season, the joyous kings, we and other embodied beings, worship Indra the lord of Devas in the festival.
81.8: On hearing the words of Nandagopa in regard to the worship of Indra, Kfsna spoke thus, in order to rouse the anger of the lord of Devas.
81.9: The four lores are Anvlksiki (Metaphysics), Tray!
81.10: O highly blessed one, the lore Varta consists of three breeding 3310113  Agriculture > trading activity and cattle
81.11: Whatever be the calling one has adopted, it should be considered as his great deity. It should be honoured and wor¬ shipped. Only that calling renders him true help.
81.12: If after reaping the fruits of one profession a man honours another, O dear father, he does not derive any thing splendid both here and hereafter.
81.13: Let our borderlands and outskirts be worshipped; our forest extends to them, the mountains mark the boundary of the forests; and the mountain is our ultimate goal.
81.14: Let a sacrifice unto the mountain or a sacrifice unto the cows be performed. What have we to do with Mahendra? The cows and the mountains are our deities.
81.15: The brahmins are devoted to Yajfias with the chanting of Mantras; the farmers are devoted to Yajnas with their plough¬ shares. We who depend upon the mountains and forests shall practise Yajnas of the mountains and cows.
81.16: Hence, let the mountain Govardhana be honoured and worshipped with all due offerings after killing the sacrificial animal in accordance with injunctions.
81.17: Let the whole quantity (of milk and milk products) of the entire colony of the cowherds be taken. Do not be anxious and worried over anything. Let the brahmins and other persons who desire be fed thereby.
81.18: O brahmins, on hearing these words of his, Nanda and other residents of the colony became delighted with their faces beaming with pleasure. They said "Well said, well said, my boy."

82.1: O brahmins, on being commended thus by the lord of Devas, those clouds let down a terrible gust of wind and downpour for the annihilation of cows. Then, O brahmins, Ear.h, sky and quarters became one as it were, due to the great showers that filled them all.
82.2: The cows began to tremble as the winds blew and the showers fell. They gave, up their lives and fell down with their heads and faces directed sideways.
82.3: O excellent brahmins, other cows stood over their calves covering them with their laps. Still other cows were deprived of their calves by the heavy downpour of water. The distressed calves exhibited their wretched faces. The chill wind made their necks shiver. They seemed to tell Krsna cf O save us, O save us" by uttering few feeble words.
82.4: On seeing the entire cowherds' colony bewildered with the cows, cowherds and cowherdesses in utter confusion, Hari thought of the means of saving them. He said.
82.5: After thinking thus, Kr?na uprooted the Govardhana mountain and playfully held it aloft with a single hand. On being advised thus by him the cowherds and the cowherdesscs who had been afflicted by the heavy downpour, entered the sheltered spot along with their cattle wealth. They kept their utensils and belongings loaded in carts.
82.6: Krsna then released the great mountain Govardhana and replaced it in its spot, closely watched by the residents of Vraja with wonderment evident in their faces.
82.7: The lord of Devas, the conqueror of enemies rode on O Kfsna, O Krsna of mighty great arms, listen, why I have come near you. This should not be misunderstood (and thought otherwise) by you.
82.8: You are indeed the great lord, the support of every¬ thing. You have incarnated on the surface of the Earth in order to remove the burden of the Earth.
82.9: The cows were saved by you by uprooting the great mountain. O heroic one, I am delighted by this extremely wonderful feat of yours. Q Krsna, I think, the purpose of Devas has been served today. This excellent mountain has been held aloft with a single hand by you.
82.10: Moreover, O Krsna, I have come near you, after being prompted by the cows saved by you. It is very much for your sake also, you are the cause of causes.
82.11: Urged by the words of cows, I shall crown you as Upendra (younger brother of Indra). You shall become Govinda, the lord of cows. Then he brought the bell from his vehicle, Airavata. Filling it with sacred waters he performed the rite of coro¬ nation.
82.12: After crowning Sri Krsna at the instance of cows, the husband of SacI, Devendra spoke to Krsna again humbly and lovingly.
82.13: I know Partha born into the Bharata family from a part of yours. As long as I continue to live on the surface of the Earth, I shall protect him. O Indra, lordofDevas, O suppressor of foes, as long as I stay on the Earth, no one will conquer Arjuna, in battle.
82.14: • Go, it does not behove you to be sad and anxious for the sake of your son. No enemy of Arjuna, howsoever great, will be too powerful in my presence.
82.15: For the sake of Arjuna I shall protect Yudhisthira and others also. When the Bharata battle is concluded I shall hand over toKunti all these persons led by Yudhisthira, (safe and) unwounded. On being assured thus the king of Devas embraced Kfsna and mounted on his elephant Airavata went back to heaven once again.
82.16: Accompanied by* cowherds and cows Krsna returned to the Vraja along the path sanctified by the loving glances of cowherd lasses.

83.1: When Iridra went away, the cowherds who had wit¬ nessed Krsna of unimpaired activities holding aloft the moun¬ tain Govardhana said to him lovingly.
83.2: O highly blessed one, from this great danger all of us and the cows have been protected by you through this activity of holding up the mountain.
83.3: (If this is only)a childish play, it is (really) unrivalled. O dear one, tending of the cows is a profession viewed at with abhorrence. But your activities are divine. How is this? May it be explained to us.
83.4: Whether you are a Deva or a Danava, whether you are a Yaksa or a Gandharva—You are our kinsman in our consideration. Obeisance be to you.
83.5: O Kesava, the love of the entire cowherds' colony in¬ cluding women and children is heaped on you. This feat is impossible to Devas too.
83.6: Your boyhood and this excessive valour, your birth amidst us, not very splendid in itself—all this, on being considered, O Krsna of immeasurable Soul, produces suspicion in us.
83.7: On being addressed thus by the cowherds, O excellent brahmins, Krsna remained silent for a while with feigned anger (in spite of his) love and said.
83.8: o cowherds, if due to your relationship with me you
83.9: I am neither a Deva nor a Gandharva, neither a Yaksa nor a Danava. I have become your kinsman. Hence, nothing other than this should be thought of me.
83.10: On hearing these words of Hari and realizing that he had feigned anger due to love, the highly blessed cowherds kept quiet. They gained in strength thereby.
83.11: The lotus-footed lord sang sweet songs in the company of Rama, pleasing to the womenfolk. He feigned that he was observing holy rites there.
83.12: On hearing the sweet and charming sound of the songs, the cowherd lasses left ofT their abodes and hurriedly came to the place where Krsna stood.
83.13: A certain cowherd lass followed his footsteps and sang slowly. Another one listened to it attentively and mentally remembered him.
83.14: A certain lass uttered "O Krsna O Krsna 5 ' and be¬ came bashful. A certain lass who was blindly in love with him went near him without shame.
83.15: Surrounded by the cowherd lasses and eager to begin the charming dance of Rasa, Govinda approved of the night, charming with the autumnal moon.
83.16: The cowherdesses were fully engrossed in the activities of Krsna. When Krsna went to a different spot those lasses walked about in the forests of Vrndavana in groups.
83.17: Eager to see Krsna, the cowherdesses wandered here and there, O brahmins, on seeing the footprint of Krsna during that night.
83.18: Thus in the course of different types of activities and sports of Krsna, the cowherd lasses became agitated simultane¬ ously and roamed about in the beautiful forest of Vrndavana. From there the cowherd lasses losing their hopes of seeing Krsna, came back to the banks of Yamuna and sang about his conduct.
83.19: Thereupon, the cowherdesses saw Krsna of unimpaired activities, the saviour of the three worlds coming to them with his face beaming like a full-blown lotus.
83.20: A certain lass became extremely delighted on seeing Krsna coming. With wide open eyes she shouted "Krsna, Krsna, Krsna". A certain lass looked at Hari with knit eyebrows over her broad forehead. She seemed to squeeze honey from his lotus face through her bee-like eyes.
83.21: A certain lass closed her eyes after seeing Govinda. Meditating on his own form she appeared to be in Yogic slumber.
83.22: Then Krsna humoured, delighted and consoled some ladies with pleasing conversations, some by glances with knit eyebrows and some by gently touching them with hands. Hari of elegant conduct sported about and diverted himself with those cowherd lasses who were delighted in their minds by means of Rasa dances enthusiastically pursued.
83.23: Then began to function a series of music with songs of autumn along with the sounds of the moving bangles.
83.24: Krsna sang about the autumnal moon, the moonlight and the lily pond, but the womenfolk of the cowherds uttered the name of Krsna alone again and again. One (of those ladies) after dancing round and round became fatigued. The heat warmed up her moving bangles. That cowherd lass put her creeper-like arms on his shoulders.
83.25: A certain cowherd lass whose arms moved about gracefully and who was an expert in singing, eulogising found pretexts, embraced and kissed him emotionally.
83.26: Hari's arms came into contact with the cheeks of cow¬ herd lasses and acted like the clouds. The downpour from these clouds was the series of sweat drops and the plants issuing therefrom were the hairs standing on end. When Krsna sang the usual songs of Rasa in highly shrill notes, the ladies shouted "Well done, Krsna, O Krsna" with notes twice as shrill.
83.27: When he went anywhere they followed him; when he moved in a circle they stood in front of him. The womenfolk of the cowherds' colony resorted to Hari both directly and inversely.
83.28: At that time Krsna sported himself together with the cowherd lasses. Even when he was away from them for a moment they felt that period of time equal to a crore of years. Though prevented by their fathers, husbands and brothers the cowherdesses who were fond of sexual intercourse delighted Krsna during the nights.
83.29: Just as Ether, Earth, fire, water, wind and Atman are present in all living beings so also he stood pervading every¬ thing.

Before they grow stronger they should be killed by me. Once they attain youth they cannot be checked from their evil activities.

84.4: After killing them I shall kill the wicked Vasudeva and Nanda too. I shall kill my father Ugrasena as well. Thereafter, I shall seize the cattle-wealth of the cow¬ herds. I shall confiscate the wealth of all those wicked ones who are desirous of killing me.
84.5: O lord of charitable gifts, excepting you all these Yada- vas are wicked in my opinion. I shall endeavour to kill them also one by one. Thereafter, I shall make this kingdom devoid of Yada- vas. As it is rid of ail thorns I shall rule it through you. Hence, O heroic one, go for my love.
84.6: You should speak to them in such a manner as to make the cowherds bring as present unto me ghee and curds the pro¬ ducts of buffalo's milk. He came to the colony of cowherds. With his hoofs he dug up pits on the ground. When he waved his manes he shook and scattered the clouds. He traversed through the aerial path of the moon and the sun.
84.7: Frightened by the neighing sound of the asura in the form of a horse the cowherds and cowherdesscs sought refuge in Krsna. On hearing their words—"Save us, O save us", Krsna spoke in a loud tone like the rumbling sound of the rain-bearing cloud.
84.8: O cowherds, do not be afraid. You belong to the clan of cowherds, why are you so afraid of Kesin? Why are you losing courage and prowess befitting the heroes?
84.9: This wicked horse has only very little strength. He is making a proud display of the loud neighing sound. He is only an ordinary messenger in the army of asuras. He is vaunting and galloping—Of what avail is this? O wicked one, come. come. I am Krsna. Just as the Pinaka-bearing lord knocked off the teeth of Pusan, so also I shall knock off thc_tceth from your mouth.
84.10: After saying thus, Krsna stood face to face with Kesin. The asura too rushed at him with a wide open mouth.
84.11: Then Krsna enlarged his arm and thrust it into the mouth of the wicked horse, Kesin. His teeth were knocked off by the arm of Krsna that was thrust into the mouth of Kesin. They looked like the bits of white clouds.
84.12: O brahmins, Krsna's arm that went into the body of Kesin became the cause of his destruction like the ailment that is neglected m the early stages by trustworthy persons (atten¬ dants, relatives or oneself;.
84.13: His lips were torn off. The corners of the mouth were made gapingly wide. He vomited frothful blood. The tendons were loosened and untied. Stretching his legs he fell on the ground and discharged dung and urine in plenty. His body was drenched in sweat. He became exhausted and ultimately ceased to struggle for life.
84.14: With his mouth torn apart by the arm of Krsna, that extremely terrible Asura fell down like a tree that is severed into two by the lightning stroke.
84.15: The two halves of the dead horse Kesin, each having two legs, one ear, one eye, one nostril and a moiety of the back and the tail shone remarkably. The sage Narada hurriedly came there seated on a cloud. On seeing Kesin killed his mind was extremely delighted.
84.16: Well done. Well done, O lord of the universe, O Acyuta! Kesin, the tormentor of heaven-dwellers, has been killed by you playfully.
84.17: (?) You were eager to bring about his death in this battle between a man and a horse. Killed by you here that wicked asura has gone to heaven. O slayer of Madhu, good rites have been performed by you in this incarnation that caused surprise in me (?) But by virtue of this action, my mind is delighted and satisfied.
84.18: O Krsna, Devas and Indra had been afraid of this horse that used to shake ofT his manes, neigh (loudly) and seethe clouds high up in the sky.
84.19: Hail to you. I shall go now. O slayer of Kesin, day O Krsna, I shall be there witnessing matches, old duels as told by you.
84.20: I shall now go, O Krsna, great task of Devas has been accomplished by you. I have been honoured by you. Hail to you. I shall go now.

87.1: Thereafter, Krsna saw a hump-backed lady in the prime of her youth, coming along the royal high-way with the vessel of unguent in her hand.
87.2: Krsna gracefully said to her:—"O lady with the eyes like the blue lotus, to whom is this unguent being taken by you? Speak the truth.
87.3: O loving one, why don't you know me? I have been employed by Kamsa in the task of preparing unguents. I am well known as Naikavakra.
87.4: The unguent ground and pasted by anyone else is not conducive to the delight of Kamsa. I am highly favoured by him and I am given much wealth too.
87.5: May this fragrant unguent beautiful and befitting kings, be given to us at least as much as will suffice our bodies.
87.6: On hearing that, she spoke to Kr?na with respect and eagerness "May it be taken." She gave them unguent enough for their bodies.
87.7: Embellished and smeared with the unguents, the two leading mainly ones shone like a white and a black cloud adorned with the rain-bow.
87.8: Krsna then pulled both of her legs and made her straight. With the body straightened she became the most excellent one among women.
87.9: In a charming ajnd graceful manner she caught hold of Krsna by his robes and said in lingering words couched in love
87.10: "I will come to your house", said Krsna to her and bade her farewell. Looking at Rama's face he laughed aloud.
87.11: With their bodies embellished and smeared with un¬ guents, clad in blue and yellow garments and with their hand¬ some features enhanced by garlands of flowers of various colours—the two went towards the chamber of bows.
87.12: The two cowherd boys have come. They are the destroyers of my life. Just in my presence they should be killed by you iii a wrestling bout.
87.13: If they are destroyed in a mutual combat by you, I will be satisfied and will give you all desired benefits. This cannot be otherwise, O strong ones.
87.14: Whether by just or unjust means, these enemies of mine should be killed by you. By their death the kingdom will be common to you both."
87.15: Then all the citizens occupied the common couches and seats and the kings occupied the royal couches and sofas along with their attendants.
87.16: The wrestlers, umpires and judges were kept in the middle of the stage by Kamsa, very near him. Kamsa himself occupied a raised sofa.
87.17: Separate couches, seats and platforms were assigned to the residents of the royal harem, the chief courtesans and the ordinary ladies of the city.
87.18: Nandagopa and other cowherds were seated in their (specially reserved) couches. Akrura and Vasudeva occupied extremities of the platform.
87.19: In the middle of the common ladies of the city was seated Devaki who was very fond of her son. Though it be the time of death, I shall see the face of my son.
87.20: "This is the boy by whom the terrible ogress Putana had been killed; he by whom the cart had been upset and the pair of Arjuna trees were broken."
87.21: "This is the boy who mounted the serpent Kaliya and danced; this is he by whom the great mountain Govardhana was lifted up and held for seven nights."
87.22: "Here is seen that Krsna the noble lord, by whom the wicked asuras Arista, Dhenuka and Kesin were playfully slain."
87.23: "This lad of great arms is Balarama, his elder brother. He sportingly goes ahead delighting the minds and eyes of the womenfolk."
87.24: "It is he who is mentioned by wisemen who survey the topics in the Puranas as follows "Gopala will redeem the entire Yadava family".
87.25: "He is that part of Visnu which has incarnated on the Earth; of Visnu who is identical with everyone; of Visnu who is the source of origin of everything. Indeed he is the dispeller of burden of the Earth".
87.26: When Rama and Krsna were described thus, the breasts of DevakI instantaneously exuded milk due to affection.
87.27: On seeing his sons, Vasudeva felt as if he was witnessing a great festival. Due to delight he dispelled the old age that had descended on him.
87.28: The ladies of the royal harem and the ordinary ladies
87.29: Krsna of unmeasured valour fought with Canura. Mustika the asura who was an expert in wrestling, fought with Balarama.
87.30: They dragged other cowherds of the same age to them¬ selves in their delight. With his eyes turned red Kamsa spoke to his men who had gathered in large.
87.31: - Let these two cowherds be forcibly removed from the the assembled group. Let the sinful Nanda be seized and bound with fetters.
87.32: Let Vasudeva also be punished in the same manner as one not old. Let all these cowherds too who vaunt and swagger along with Krsna, be punished suitably.
87.33: Be pleased, O lord of Devas, O most excellent one, O lord, O Kesava, favouring us you have lifted us up.
87.34: Since after being propitiated by me the lord has incar¬ nated in my house for destroying the wicked ones, thereby our race is sanctified.
87.35: You remain within living beings. You are stationed within living beings, O soul of everyone, it is from you that the past and future function, invariably.
87.36: O Acyuta, identical with Devas, O incomprehensible and unimaginable one, you are worshipped in the course of a Yajna. O lord of Yajnas, you are the Yajna and the performer of Yajna.
87.37: O son ofDevakl, the fact that out of affection, my mind is full of vague notions in respect of you is great decep¬ tion.
87.38: You are the maker of all living beings. You have neither beginning nor end. Where is the tongue pertaining to me, a mere human being, which says— c O son'.
87.39: By what expedient, excepting Maya, will that person be born of us, O lord of the Universe, that person from whom all this universe has evolved?
87.40: How can that lord be borne by a female human being, that lord in whom the entire universe consisting of mobile and immobile beings lias been established? How can he be made to lie down in the womb or in the lap?
87.41: O great lord, be pleased. Protect the universe. Since you are having the partial incarnation you are not my son, O soul of the great lord, O lord of the universe, why do you delude the mind of every one from Brahman to an ordinary tree.
87.42: My eyes had been deluded by Maya. I had the feeling "Here is my son." Much afraid of Kamsaat that time, you were taken to the cowherds' colony. O lord of cows, you entered then my intellect, even as I was afraid and agitated due to the enemies.

88.2: Then Karhsa's wives surrounded the dead body of Kamsa and lamented. His mothers too were fully overwhelmed by sorrow and misery.
88.3: They were upset in various ways. They were agitated due to repentance. Krsna consoled them. His own eyes became turbid due to tears.
88.4: He then released Ugrasena from prison. He crowned Ugrasena whose son had been killed. He crowned him in his own kingdom.
88.5: After being crowned in the kingdom he, the lion among the descendants of Yadu clan, performed the obsequies of his son as well as of others who were killed there.
88.6: Thus urged, the wind god went to Indra and spoke everything to him. Indra gave the assembly hall Sudharma to Vayu.
88.7: All those leading Yadus, having Krsna's arms for support enjoyed that divine assembly hall decorated with jewels and brought over there by Vayu.
88.8: They accepted his discipleship. They were duly en¬ gaged in serving the preceptor. To all the people they thus practically demonstrated their proper conduct.
88.9: Within sixtyfour days and nights they learned the science of Archery alongwith its secrets and digests. O brah¬ mins, it was miraculous indeed.
88.10: Considering their super-human activity that could not at all have been imagined (in persons of their age) Sandipani thought that the moon and the sun had come to him.
88.11: The moment they were uttered, (the two brothers) learned the Mantras of all miraculous missiles. They said— "What monetary gift should be paid as the preceptor's fees? That may be mentioned."
88.12: Observing their ability to act beyond the pale of sense-organs the highly intelligent preceptor requested (the resuscitation) of his son who was dead in the holy centre of Prabhasa on the shore of the briny sea.
88.13: Equipped with their arms they went to the briny ocean. They said to the sea—"May the son of our preceptor be restored".

90.1: O brahmins, Syala called a brahmin of the cowherds colony (named) Gargya by the (ignoble remark) Sandha
90.2: Thereupon, the infuriated brahmin went to Southern territory and performed a penance. He was desirous of a son who would be a terror to the Yadavas.
90.3: The \ avanesa (a Greek King) who had no son honour¬ ed him. As a result of sexual intercourse withhis wife a son of fiery splendour was born to him.
90.4: Proud and arrogant by virtue of his prowess, he asked about the powerful kings on the Earth. Narada told him about the Yadavas.
90.5: After thinking thus Kjrsna begged of the great ocean a piece twelve Yojana. He created the city of Dvaraka there.
90.6: When the army (of Kalayavana) encamped outside Mathura, he came out without any weapon and the Yavana saw him.
90.7: The Yavana also entered the cave. He saw a man lying on a bed. Thinking him to be Krsna, the wicked Yavana kicked him with his foot.
90.8: That king had taken part in the battle between Devas and Asuras and defeated Asuras. He had to remain for many nights without sleep and so was distressed. He requested Suras for the boon of slumber.
90.9: After reducing that sinner he looked at Krsna and said—"Who are you?" Krsna said: "I am born of the lunar race.
90.10: You are everything viz-oceans, mountains, rivers, forests, Earth, sky, wind, water, fire, you are the highest being.
90.11: O lord, miseries alone were taken up by me as pleasures, like the mirages that are understood as water-reser¬ voirs. They were conducive to my agony alone.
90.12: O lord, even Devas attaining the goal of the common world became desirous of help from me. Where is permanent happiness (available)?
90.13: Without propitiating you, the basis and source of origin of all the worlds, by whom is permanent happiness attained?

91.1: Eulogised thus by that intelligent Mucukunda, the lord of all living beings, the lord who has no beginning or death spoke thus.
91.2: O lord of men, go to divine worlds as desired by you. You will be strengthened by my grace and your prosperity and prowess will be unimpeded.
91.3: After enjoying the great divine pleasures, you will be born in a great family. By my favour you will be able to remem¬ ber your previous births. Thereafter, you will attain salvation. Thus blessed by the lord the king bowed to Acyuta; the lord of the worlds came out of the cave. Then' he saw short- statured men;
91.4: The king understood that the Kaliyuga had arrived. He went to the abode of Nara and Narayana in order to perform penance (on the mountain) Gandhamidana.
91.5: Slaying the enemy by means of a stratagem, Krsna captured his army shining with horses, elephants and chariots After bringing it to Dvaravatihe offered it toUgrasena. (Thereby) the army of the Yadus had no fear of the onslaught of enemies.
91.6: O leading brahmins, having subdued all quarrels Bala- deva became eager to see his kinsmen and so went to the cow¬ herds' colony of Nanda.
91.7: As before, the conqueror of enemies spoke to the cowherds and cowherdlasses with affection and respect. The cowherds spoke many pleasing words to Balarama. Some cowherdesses spoke joyously in their love and others spoke with malice.
91.8: Other cowherdesses asked thus "Is Krsna the lover of womenfolk of the city happy? Is he agitated by stirring emotions of love.
91.9: Does Krsna ever remember our following him and singing alongwith him? Will he come here at least once to see his mother? Father, mother, brother, husband and kinsmen who is not abandoned by us for his sake. (But) he load been un¬ grateful.
91.10: Still, does Krsna ever (mention) anything about his coming here? Nectar-like words must be uttered by you.
91.11: He appears to be devoid of love towards us because his rnindis attached to the ladies of the city. It seems it will be difficult to sec him." The cowherdlasses were consoled by Rama through gentle and sweet messages of Krsna couched in loving emo¬ tions and devoid of arrogance. The notes were as sweet as honey.
91.12: As before Balarama continued funny stories and jokes with the cowherds whose minds were attracted by Krsna, the cowherds who were the residents of Vraja.

92.1: O wine, you have always been liked by (Balarama) of great prowess, O auspicious one, go now for his joy and enjoyment of pleasures.
92.2: Thus advised by him Varuni (wine) stationed herself in the hollow of a Kadamba tree growing on-the banks of Yamuna in Vrndavana.
92.3: Roaming about that spot Balarama inhaled the inten- sive odour of wine. After smelling it he experienced the delight that he previously used to have in wine.
92.4: O sages, thereafter, Balarama saw a current of liquor suddenly falling from Kadamba. He derived great joy there¬ from.
92.5: He drank it joyously in the company of cowherds and cowlici desses while experts in songs and instrumental music sang elegantly.
92.6: Shining with the pearl-like drops of sweat due to excessive heat and fatigue he became agitated and said -;t O Yamuna, come hither. I wish to take my bath".
92.7: The river disregarded those words of inebriated person. She did not approach him. The infuriated Balarama (there¬ upon) seized his ploughshare.
92.8: Agitated due to inebriation he caught hold of her by the tip of his ploughshare - "O evil-minded one, won't you come, won't you come? Then go elsewhere as you please".
92.9: Dragged by him suddenly the river left her usual path and flooded the forest where Balarama was present.
92.10: She approached him in an embodied form. Due to fear her eyes were agitated. She said to him "O you having lionclub as your weapon, be pleased, leave me off".
92.11: He said "If you disregard me in spite of my heroism and strength I shall split you into a thousand bits with the blows of my ploughshare".
92.12: Having aborned himself with the blue lotus, embelli¬ shing himself with the beautiful ear-ring and clad in blue garments, the glorious one shone with splendour.
92.13: Thus embellished, Rama sported there in the cow¬ herds' colony. After two months he went to Dvaraka.

93.1: Krsna loved Rukmini and the lady of beautiful smiles loved him in return. Due to hatred, Rukmin did not give her to the discus-bearing lord.
93.2: Urged by Jarasandha and Rukmin together, Bhismaka of great exploit gave Rukmini to Sisupala.
93.3: Then for the purpose of marriage the kings led by Jarasandha, and Sisupala went to Kundina the city of Bhismaka.
93.4: Surrounded by Balarama and other scions of the Yadu, Krsna went to Kundina to witness the marriage of Sisupala, the king of Cedi.
93.5: On the sixth day after his birth, O brahmins, Kala- sambara kidnapped Pradyumna from the lying-in-chamber thinking—"O this one will be my killer".
93.6: Taking the boy with him he hurled him into the briny sea, infested with crocodiles, the awful abode of sparks that abounded in eddies and whirlpools generated by billows.
93.7: As the boy fell down there a fish caught hold of him. Though burned by its gastric fire the boy did not die.
93.8: O brahmins, this fish alongwith other fishes was caught by fishermen and offered to Sambara the most excellent one among the Asuras.
93.9: His wife named Mayavati, the uncensured queen of his household, supervised over the work of cooks.

94.2: O brahmins, to attend her marriage Rama and other descendants of Yadu went to Rukmin's city named Bhojakata, along, with Lord Krsna.
94.3: After the marriage of noble son of Pradyumna was concluded, Kalinga king and others spoke these words to Rukmin.

94.6: Then, O brahmins, exhibiting all his teeth, the foolish overlord of Kalinga laughed at Bala. The haughty Rukmin spoke then:
94.7: O members of the assembly, this Balarama devoid of learning has been defeated by me in the game of dice. He is not conversant with either the manner of fighting or the lore of the game.
94.8: On seeing the king of Kalinga with the teeth in his mouth fully exhibited, and Rukmin indulging in harsh words, Balarama became infuriated.
94.9: With his mind full of fury Balarama put up the stake at a crore of gold coins. Rukmin too accepted it: He threw the dice for that purpose.
94.10: Baladevawon the stake. He said to him loudly "This is won by me".
94.11: "It is true that this stake was announced by you. But it had not been accepted or approved of by me. That being the case if (you say) you have won how (can't I say that) I have won?
94.12: Then loud resonant words rose up in the sky aggravat¬ ing the fury of noble Baladeva.
94.13: The speech in the firmament said: "The stake is won by Baladeva. What is uttered by Rukmin is false. Certain things are accepted through actions even without mentioning words."
94.14: Then Bala of great strength got up with his eyes turned red due to fury. With the dice board itself he hit and killed Rukmin.
94.15: With great force he held the king of Kalinga who was throbbing and trembling. In his fury he broke his teeth with which he had openly laughed at him.
94.16: The infuriated Bala seized a great column of gold and killed those kings who belonged to his side.

95.1: O lord, all miseries have been subdued by you, the lord of Devas, though stationed in the form of a human being.
95.2: When the three worlds have been saved by your excellent intellect as well as brawny baton-like arms, the
95.3: O lord, it behoves you to pursue efforts and counter¬ measures after listening to the reason for which I have come now.
95.4: O suppressor of enemies, this son of Bhumi named Naraka
95.5: After killing Devas, Siddhas, kings, and others that Asura imprisoned their daughters in his own palace.
95.6: He has taken away the umbrella of Pracetas that exudes water. He has removed the Maniparvata, peak of the Mandara.
95.7: That Asura has taken away the illustrious ear-rings of my mother Aditi, the ear-rings that exude nectar. He now desires to take possession of my elephant Airavata.
95.8: O lord, I have told you about his evil activities. What steps should be taken by way of remedy may be pondered over by yourself.
95.9: On hearing this, lord Krsna, son of DevakI, smiled and caught hold of the hand of Indra. He then got up from the excellent seat.
95.10: He then rode on Garuda who traversed through the sky. He kept Satyabhama also on its back and went to the city of Pragjyotisa.
95.11: Even as the residents of Dvaraka watched him, the delighted Indra mounted his elephant Airavata and went to heaven.
95.12: For a hundred Yojanas all round the city of Pragjyo¬ tisa, the entire place was covered with terrible nooses in order to ward off the army of enemies.
95.13: Lord Krsna hurled his discus Sudarsana and cut off those nooses. Then the asura Mura got up. Kesava killed him.
95.14: By the fire from the sharp edges of his discus Hari burned seven thousand sons of Mura as though they were mere moths,
95.15: O brahmins, after killing Mura, Hayagrlva and Pancajana the intelligent lord hastened to Pragjyotisa.
95.16: By hurling his discus the discus-bearing lord, the power¬ ful destroyer of asuras, split Naraka into two, Naraka, son of the Earth, who was hurling weapons and missiles on him.
95.17: He had been given to me by you and now has been struck down by you. Take back these two ear-rings and protect his children.
95.18: You are the creator, re-creator, annihilator, eternal source of origin and one whose form is identical with that of the universe. O Acyuta, how ami to eulogise you?.
95.19: You are the one all-pervading and the pervaded; deed, the doer and the thing done. You are the Atman, the inner soul of all living beings. O Acyuta, how can I eulogise you?
95.20: You are the Supreme Atman, the innermost soul, the soul of living beings, the eternal lord. These are not your praises. They are the statements of facts. How shall anyone go about (this act of eulogy)?
95.21: O lord, the soul of all-living beings, be pleased. May what is done by Naraka be excused for making him free from defects. My son has already been struck down.
95.22: "So be it", the lord said to the Earth. O excellent sages, the conceiver and creator of the living beings took up jewels from the residence of Naraka.

96.1: Playfully carrying the umbrella of Varuna, the jewel mountain and bearing lord Krsna on his back accompanied by his wife, Garuda went ahead.
96.2: Lord Krsna reached the gateway of heaven and blew the conch. Then Devas approached the lord along with the vessels full of materials of worship.
96.3: After being worshipped by Devas, Krsna entered the abode of the mother of Devas that had the shape of the peak of white mountain. After entering it he saw Aditi.
96.4: Accompanied by Indra he bowed to her. The lord gave her the excellent earrings and intimated to her the death of Naraka.
96.5: Obeisance to you, O lotus-eyed one, O lord causing fearlessness to devotees, O lord, the eternal Atman, O Atman of living beings, O Atman of everything,© creator of living beings.
96.6: O lord, if one takes the non-Atman to be the Atman, this misconception is your Maya. It is from this that the ideas of T, 'Mine* etc. emerge.
96.7: O lady of fine eye-brows, due to my favour you will never have old age or deformity. O lady of blameless limbs, you will enjoy all worldly pleasures.
96.8: Permitted by Aditi, the king of Devas duly worshipped the lord with adequate reverence.
96.9: Then, O excellent ones, Kfsna accompanied by Satya- bhama visited the divine gardens and parks such as Nandana.
96.10: You seek for this Parijata out of foolishness. Who will go out safe and secure if he takes this with him? O Krsna, the lord of Devas will indeed be furious over this.
96.11: The immortal ones will follow Indra with the thunder¬ bolt raised up in his hand. Hence, O Acyuta, enough of your attempts to quarrel with Devas. Scholars do not praise that action which is very bitter in its result.
96.12: The guards of the park who were addressed thus, went to §aci and told her what they were told. Saci then encouraged her husband the over-lord of Devas.
96.13: Then Indra stood ready with the thunderbolt in his hand. Devas also stood in readiness holding their weapons such as iron clubs, sword and tridents.
96.14: Then lord of the worlds playfully split each of the missiles and weapons discharged by Devas, into a thousand bits.
96.15: Garuda snatched the noose of the king of waters (i.e. Varuna), split it into bits like the body of a young serpent and moved about.
96.16: The lord, the son of Devaki, struck down on to the ground the staff discharged by Yama. It was broken when he hurled his iron club at it.
96.17: The lord Krsna smashed the palanquin of the god of wealth into minute bits like gingelly seeds. The sun' and the moon lost their prowess.as it was destroyed by a single glance of the lord..
96.18: The Sadhyas, Visvedevas, Maruts and Gandharvas were sent up into the sky like the cotton bits from a Salmali tree by the Sarhga-bearing lord through his arrows.
96.19: Garuda killed and ate Devas and Upadevas by means of his beak, wings and claws.
96.20: Then Indra, the lord of Devas, and lord Krsna, the slayer of Madhu showered each other with a thousand arrows like two clouds by heavy downpours.
96.21: In the utter confusion obtaining there, Garuqla fought with Airavata and lord.Krsna with Devas accompanied by Indra.
96.22: When weapons and missiles were split and scattered, Indra hastily seized the thunderbolt and Krsna took up his discus Sudarsana.
96.23: On seeing the king of Devas and Sri Krsna holding up their thunderbolt and discus respectively the whole of the uni¬ verse consisting of mobile and immobile beings raised a hue and cry.
96.24: Lord Krsna caught hold of thunderbolt hurled by Indra. Without releasing his discus he told him c stay, stay'.
96.25: As the king of Devas lost his thunderbolt, as his vehicle was wounded by Garuda, he became inclined to run away then. Satyabhama spoke to him.
96.26: O Indra, enough of your endeavour. It does not behove you to be ashamed. Let this Parijata tree be taken away. Let Devas be rid of pain. On account of her excessive pride and arrogance SacI did not view me with reverence as I went to her house. Nor did she honour me.
96.27: O brahmins, when addressed thus the king of Devas re¬ turned and said to her:

97.1: O excellent brahmins, eulogised thus by the king of Devas, lord Krsna laughed and spoke in an emotionally majes- tic manner.
97.2: You are Indra, the king of Devas. O lord of the universe, we are mortals. The crime committed by me should be excused by you.
97.3: May this Parijata tree be taken to its proper site. O Indra, it was at the instance of Satya that it was taken by me.
97.4: Take back this thunderbolt which had been hurled at me by you. O Indra, it is your own weapon that pierces enemies.
97.5: O Lord, why do you try to delude me by saying "I am a mortal". We know you; we are conversant with the infinite happiness.
97.6: As you are, so you are, O lord of the universe. O lord, you are firmly fixed in your work. O slayer of Asuras, you re¬ move thorns of the universe.
97.7: O Krsna, may this Parijata tree be taken to Dvaravatl. Except with you this will not remain anywhere else in the mortal world.
97.8: After saying "So be it" to the lord of Devas Sri K r sna came to the Earth, eulogised by the liberated Siddhas, Gan- dharvas and sages.
97.9: Taking the excellent tree with him, Krsna hastened.

99.3: Lord Krsna said thus to Mahesvara Jvara—"Those who remember our fight between us shall be free from fever. After saying this lord Krsna went away. Then the lord defeated and destroyed the five fires. Visnu playfully smashed the army of Asuras.

99.9: O Krsna, O Krsna, O lord of the universe, I know (hat you are Purusottama the great lord, the great Atman the greatest being without beginning or without end. 99.10: He has grown old in serving me and having my support. O unchanging one, it is not your fault. (?) Boons have been granted to this Daitya by me. Hence, I request fo. your forbearance.

101.1: O sage, we wish to hear again about the exploits of the intelligent Balarama. It behoves you to recount his heroism unto us.
101.2: His exploits, such as dragging Yamuna have already been heard by us here. Hence, O blessed one, kindly recount anything else which Bala performed.
101.3: O sages, listen to the activities carried out by Rama the infinite one, the unmeasurable one, the incarnation ofSesa, the holder of the Earth.
101.4: Samba the heroic son of Jambavatl forcefully abducted Duryodhana's daughter whose Svayamvara was awaited.
101.5: Then the infuriated Karna, Duryodhana and others including Bhlsma and Drona of great prowess bound him after conquering him.
101.6: On hearing about it, O sages, the Yadavas became
101.7: Bala stopped them and spoke to them although his words were indistinct through inebriation:—
101.8: Then Balarama went to Hastinapura. He camped in the middle of a park at the outskirts of the city. He did not enter it.
101.9: On coming to know that Balarama had arrived, Duryodhana and others brought unto him by way of presents, greetings, along with Arghya and water for drinking.
101.10: After duly accepting those things he said to the Kauravas—"It is Ugrasena's order—Release Samba quickly".
101.11: O excellent brahmins, on hearing his words, Bhlsma, Drona, Karna, Duryodhana and others became angry.
101.12: Bahllka and all other kings too, were angry on seeing Balarama who had the threshing rod for his weapon and realizing that the race of Yadu did not deserve a kingdom, they said:—
101.13: If even Ugrasena can pass orders on Kauravas, enough of the white umbrellas and ornaments befitting kings.
101.14: Hence, go back, O Balarama. Neither at your bidding will we release Samba whose activities are unjust.
101.15: Formerly, Kukuras and Andhakas used to bow unto us, for we are worthy of that honour. Now-a-days that usual obeisance is not made. What is this commanding attitude of a servant towards a master?
101.16: After saying this the Kauravas remained adamant. They did not release Krsna's son. After making this unanimous decision they entered Hastinapura.
101.17: Maddened by the anger originating from the insult, Balarama lifted up his rugged ploughshare and rolled it.
101.18: Alas, the insignificant wicked haughty Kauravas wish to rule over us. It is brought abput by adverse time.
101.19: The womenfolk of the servants of Ugrasena wear bun¬ ches of flower, of Parijata tree, still he is not a king for these people.
101.20: Let Ugrasena, the lord of kings stay by. I shall go to that city after making the Earth devoid of Kauravas.

102.1: O holy sage, explain the number of Parardha as it has been mentioned before, and by doubling which the natural re¬ absorption has to be realized. Fifteen Kalas make a Nadika. In the calculation of time by means of the measurement of water it is equivalent to half of thirteen Palas (6£ Palas of water trickling down through a hole may take a Nadika of time i.e. 24 minutes to flow out completely).
102.2: O excellent brahmins, two Nadikas make one Muhurta (48 minutes). A day of twentyfour hours consists of thirty Muhurtas and thirty days make a month. Twelve months make a year and this constitutes a peiiod of a day and a night in the heaven. Three hundred and sixty human years make one divine year.
102.3: Twelve thousand divine years make a set of four Yugas. A thousand sets of four Yugas are considered to be one day of Brahma. Then, O excellent sages, almost all of those earthly
102.4: Then the imperishable lord Krsna assumes the form of Rudra and endeavours to keep the subjects within himself for the purpose of annihilation. After drinking up the water present in the elements and living beings, O brahmins, he makes the entire surface of the Earth dried up and withered.
102.5: He dries up oceans, rivers, mountains and mountain springs. He sucks up the water that is present in the nether worlds too. As every particle of water vanishes there will be seven suns, each of a thousand rays and they become increased in size due to their watery diet.
102.6: Blazing from beneath and above, O brahmins, those seven suns burn up the three worlds along with the nether worlds. On being burnt by those blazing suns, the three worlds, along with the extensive area of mountains, trees and oceans, become devoid of viscidity.
102.7: Then the entire area of the three worlds, O brahmins, has all the trees and watery parts dried up. The Earth attains the shape of the back of a tortoise. Thereafter lord Hara, the annihilator of all created be¬ ings, terrible like black fire, burns the nether worlds from below by means of the hot breath of the serpent Sesa.
102.8: From there also people proceed ahead to Janaloka on being scorched by the great sunshine ten times more power¬ ful. They are desirous of a supreme abode. After burning the entire universe, O excellent sages, the lord in the guise of Rudra, produces clouds by means* of breath expelled from his mouth.
102.9: Thereafter, rise up in the sky the Samvartaka clouds Some of these clouds are like a collyrium mountain; some are like the elephant Kumuda. Some are smoky in colour! Some are yellow.
102.10: Some are turmeric; some resemble the exudation of lac juice; some appear like lapis lazuli; and some are like sapphire. Some resemble a conch shell and others the turner's lathe; some are like Jati flower (white jasmine) and some are like Kunda. Some are scarlet coloured like the tiny insect Indragopa (glow-worm) and some are like Manahs'ita (?)
102.11: Some of the terrible clouds rise up like the petals of a Others resemble the apartments on the tops of houses; some are like the dry tracts of ground. They are huge in body and loud In their sound; they cover the sky completely.

103.1: How did Krsna exterminate his family under the pre¬ text of the curse of brahmins? How did he give up his human form? O messenger, I know fully well what you say. But the destruction of Yadavas is only just started by me.
103.2: If they remain uncxlerminated, they will constitute a great burden unto the Earth. Hence I shall hurriedly bring that down within seven nights. In the same manner as it had been taken from the ocean I shall replace Dvaraka in the ocean, exterminate Yada¬ vas and then return to heaven.
103.3: I shall cast off my human body too, assisted by Sam- karsana. It should be considered by the leader of Devas that I have come there. Thus informed by Vasudcva O sages, the divine messenger bowed to him and went to heaven near the king of Devas.
103.4: Day and night the lord witnessed evil omens in hea¬ ven, on Earth and in the sky as well, indicating the destruction of Dvaraka. On seeing them he said to Yadavas—"See the extre¬ mely terrible evil omens. In order to subdue these, we shall go to Prabhasa. Do not delay".
103.5: After finishing this family I shall go to Heaven. T e sea will engulf Dvaraka in its flood when it has been abandon¬ ed by me. Thus advised and urged by Krsna, Uddhava bowed to liim and went to the abode of Nara and Narayana.
103.6: Then Yadavas, O brahmins, got into fast moving chariots and went to Prabhasa alongwith Krsna, Balarama and
103.7: Krsna restrained them. They thought that he was one who had come to assist them. They bit and struck one another. The infuriated Krsna seized a fistful of Eraka from them. Thus the iron club became the fistful of iron for their destruction.
103.8: As an Assailant he killed all Yadavas. Suddenly they too approached him and hit one another. Others also did like¬ wise.
103.9: Then O excellent brahmins, even as Daruka went on watching, observing, Jaitra, the chariot of the discus-bearing lord was dragged by the horses through the middle of the ocean. The discus Sarnga, quivers, conch and the sword circumambulated him and went away along the solar path.
103.10: O excellent brahmins, within a moment Yadavas were destroyed except the mighty-armed Krsna and Daruka.

105.1: Arjuna found out the cast off physical bodies of Krsna and Balarama and performed the requisite consecratory rites. He did the same for others too.
105.2: The eight crowned queens of Krsna, RukminI and others, took the dead body of Krsna and entered fire*
105.3: Revati the excellent lady, embraced the body of Bala¬ rama and entered the blazing fire which cooled and delighted her by the mere touch of her body.
105.4: On hearing about this, Ugrasena, Anakadundubhi, DevakI and RohinI entered fire.
105.5: Arjuna performed their funeral rites in accordance with the injunctions. Taking all the people and Vajra with him he left Dvaraka.
105.6: Thousands of wives of Krsna went out of Dvaravatl. Looking after Vajra and the people, the son of Kunti went ahead slowly.
105.7: O brahmins, the assembly chamber Sudharma, that had been brought to the mortal world by Kisnawent back to heaven. So also the Parijata tree..
105.8: The great ocean flooded Dvaraka. The sea did not engulf the house of the most excellent one among the descendants of Yadu. This was the only thing it did not envelop in its waters.
105.9: O excellent sages, in the land ofPancanada (watered by five rivers), equipped with much of wealth and foodgrains, Arjuna made arrangements for the residence of all the people.
105.10: Tnereafter Dasyus who hurled lumps of clay and who struck with their staffs rushed at those womenfolk whose hus¬ bands had been killed. They attacked them in their thousands. Turning back, the son of Kunti spoke to the Abhiras laughingly.
105.11: When the arrows were exhausted Arjuna struck them with the tip of his bow. O brahmins, at the blow the Dasyus laughed derisively.
105.12: Arjuna became dejected saying—"Alas; Alas, I have been abandoned by that lord." He lamented.
105.13: That bow, those miraculous missiles, that chariot and those horses—all these are destroyed at one'stroke like the chari¬ table gift to one who is not learned in the Vedas.
105.14: My superior powers and those of Bhimawere certainly effected by Lord Kjrsna. Without him, I have been conquered by the cowherds. How can it happen otherwise?
105.15: Saying thus, Arjuna went to Indraprastha. There he crowned as king, the Yadava scion Vajra.
105.16: Arjuna saw there the highly blessed sage Vyasa with his abode in the forest. He approached him humbly and saluted the sage.
105.17: He who had been our strength, our splendour, our prowess, our exploit, our glory, our lustre—lord Kna—has left us.
105.18: To me the Earth appears like a lady who has lost her blooming youth, whose splendour is destroyed and whose lustre has vanished. O dear one, I am not the only one to suffer from the bereavement of the discus-bearing lord.
105.19: Due to the power and magnificence of Krsna I was able to kill Bhlsma and others. I was like fire and they were like moths. But today, without lord Krsna, I have been defeated by cowherds. O great sage, thousands of helpless ladies have been carried off, in spite of my endeavour, by the Dasyus who had batons for their weapons.
105.20: All the womenfolk of Krsna, while being brought over here by me, have been carried away by the cowherds who carried sticks as their weapons.
105.21: On hearing the words of the noble-minded Arjuna, who Enough of your being ashamed, O Arjuna, it does not behove you to bewail. Understand that the working of time in all living beings is like this.
105.22: Formerly, the Earth that had been afflicted by burden had gone to Devas. It was for that purpose that Visnu who could assume any form that he desired had taken up incarnation.
105.23: That task has been achieved, the kings have been killed. The family of Vrsnis and Andhakas has been duly finished. This lord of Devas performs creation at the beginning and sustains during its maintenance. He is competent to annihi¬ late as well, as has been done now.
105.24: Hence, O Arjuna, you must not feel aggrieved due to this discomfiture. At the moment of creative activity men will have exploits.
105.25: That lord, the lord of the universe, permeates other bodies and performs the task of dissolving all living beings in the end. During the origin of this creative process the lord was your ally, O son of Kuntl. At the close of created beings those who are viewed with sympathy by the lord had been your adversaries.
105.26: Who could have believed at the beginning that you could kill Kauravas including Bhisma? Who could have believ¬ ed your discomfiture at the hands of cowherds?
105.27: O Arjuna, Rambha, Tilottama and hundreds and thou¬ sands of other ladies eulogised and praised that great soul. They praised the sage who wore weighty matted hair and who was standing immersed in water up to his neck. With humility they bent down their heads. They were eager in repeating the hymns.
105.28: They eulogised him so much that he became pleased with them. O most excellent among the descendants of Kuru, they eulogised that most excellent brahmin.
105.29: O highly blessed ladies, I am delighted. Whatever is wished for by you, may be requested for from me. I shall grant it even if it.is very difficult to grant. Hence, O Arjuna, even the least bit of sorrow need not be felt by you. Everything has already been ordained by the lord of all.
105.30: Your strength, splendour, prowess and greatness have been condensed by the lord desirous of annihilating you all.

106.1: O excellent sage, the rare manifestation and the diverse activities of lord Krsna as well as Balarama in the world have been mentioned by you.
106.2: Listening to the story of the lord we are not contented. We wish to hear about the other manifestations of the lord of the universe.
106.3: We do not know his full conduct nor the details of the process whereby the incarnation took place. We do not know the extent of the existence of Gunas and Karmans in him. We do not know the extent of his will in the causation thereof.
106.4: I shall mention the greatness of Vasudeva, the con¬ duct of life of the highly intelligent one, for the welfare of Devas and mortal beings as well as the origin of the worlds.
106.5: The supreme Atman manifests himself on many occa¬ sions. I shall recount the manifestations that are divine, sacred and endowed with good qualities.
106.6: The lord of Devas, the lord of universe, who sleeps for the period of a thousand sets of four Yugas, manifests himself against some (specific) task after the thousand sets of four Yugas are completed.
106.7: O you of good holy rites, I am pleased wtih your penance. Welfare unto you. Choose a boon. Obtain your cherished desires.
106.8: O dear one, all these divine and wonderful boons have been granted to you by me. O dear one, you will attain all these desires.
106.9: After saying this, lord Brahma immediately went to his abode frequented by the brahminical sage.
106.10: On hearing about the granting of boon, Devas, Nagas, Gandharvas and sages approached him.
106.11: O lord, with this boon, that Asura will harass us. Hence, O lord, be pleased, let the manner of his destruction be also thought of.
106.12: O lord, you are the self-born lord, you are the cause of all living beings, you are the creator of Havyas and Kavyas. You Are the unmanifest being. You are certainly Prakrti.
106.13: O Devas, the fruit of penance must of course be obtain- ed by him. But as the benefits of penance are exhausted lord Visnu will slay him.
106.14: On hearing these words of the lotus-born Brahma Devas felt joyous. They returned to their divine abodes.
106.15: Immediately after he had obtained the boon, the asura Hiranyakasipu became haughty and he harassed his subjects.
106.16: He overpowered and insulted the highly blessed sages of holy rites, interested in truthfulness and piety and of subdued sense-organs.
106.17: That great Asura defeated Devas stationed in heaven. He kept the three worlds under his control and lived in heaven.
106.18: Whenever that asura became haughty due to his obtaining the boon he roamed over the Earth. He made asuras worthy of shares in the Yajnas and Devas, unworthy of shares in the same.
106.19: O lord of Devas, save us today from the fear of Hiran- yakasipu. Indeed you are our greatest lord. You are our greatest preceptor.
106.20: O most excellent one among Devas, you are indeed the supreme creator of all of us, Brahma and others. O lord, with the eyes resembling thepetals of a full blown lotus devoid of impurities, O lord, the destroyer of the enemy hosts, be our refuge for the destruction of the race of Diti.
106.21: O immortal ones, cast off your fear. I grant you all, fearlessness. O Devas, you will regain heaven as before without delay.
106.22: I shall kill this asura along with his attendants. I shall kill this leading Danava haughty on account of his acquiring the boon that he cannot be killed by the leading immortal
106.23: After saying this to the chiefs of Devas and bidding
106.24: A further manifestation of Visnu the great Atman, in the nature of a living being, is well known as Dattatreya. He was equipped with great forbearance.
106.25: O lord of the Earth, you will protect the entire Earth. Engaged in battle you become so dazzling that you will not be stared at by the enemy.
106.26: This glorious and auspicious manifestation of Visnu has been recounted to you. There is another manifestation of the great Atman namely Jamadagnya Parasurama.
106.27: In the course of this manifestation the lord Parasurama killed king Sahasrarjuna in battle. Previously he had been invincible to the enemies in battle by the prowess of his thousand arms.
106.28: The Earth where crores of Ksatriyas remained scatte¬ red about, the Earth that is adorned by the mountains Meru and Mandara was rid of Ksatriyas twentyone* times by the lord.
106.29: After making the Earth devoid of Ksatriyas, Para¬ surama of great fame performed a horse sacrifice in order to dispel his sins.
106.30: Rama the lord of the living beings killed Ravana who had a huge body, who was very powerful and who resembled a mass of clouds.
106.31: For the sake of Sugrlva, Bali the powerful lord of monkeys was killed in battle and Sugrlva was crowned in his place.
106.32: Janasthana: A part of DaijiJaka forest which lies in the basin of Godavari. Rama had lived in this forest with Sita and Laksmana for a long time during the period of his exile.
106.33: The great Asura, the haughty son of Madhu, the Danava named Lavana, the heroic demon, proud of his boons was killed in the forest (named) Madhuvana.
106.34: The tiger among men killed Viradha and Kabandha, the Raksasas of terrible exploits who had been formerly two Gandharvas deluded by imprecation.
106.35: In the battle Rama killed his enemies by means of arrows, that had the lustre of fire, sun-rays and lightning streaks, that had the tail ends fitted with feathers of various kinds made of molten gold and the strength of which was like that of the thunderbolt of Mahendra.
106.36: Weapons were given to him by Visvaraitra the intelli¬ gent sage for slaying the enemies who could not be assailed even by Devas.
106.37: Formerly, when a certain sacrifice yvas performed by Janaka the great Atman, the great bow belonging to Mahesvara was broken by him even as he playfully and sportingly touched it.
106.38: After performing these tasks Rama the most excellent among the virtuous performed ten horse-sacrifices where flesh was offered to the deities.
106.39: No widow lamented. There were no calamities. Every¬ thing was auspicious when Rama was ruling over the earth.
106.40: No living being had any fear from water, fire, wind or blows (of any sort). Old men never performed the funeral rites of boys (i.e. boys never died before old men).
106.41: The Ksatriyas were devoted to the Brahmins. The Vaisyas were devoted to the Ksatriyas. The Sudras served the three castes without any pride or egotism.
106.42: Women did not stray from their husbands; the hus¬ band did not stray from his wife. The entire universe was restrained and subdued. The earth was rid of robbers.
106.43: Thousands ofarmsofBana of miraculous activities were cut off. Naraka was killed in the war. So also Yavana of great strength.
106.44: All the jewels of the kings were taken away by him
106.45: The following manifestation of the great Atman is conducive to the welfare of the world. It is the manifestation of Kalki named Visnuyasas also. It will occur in the village of Sambhala.

107.1: O sage, we are not satiated by hearing about holy meritorious rites. Greatly sung by you they are like nectar. Our enthusiasm is further increased.
107.2: O sage, you know everything, origin and dissolution of living beings and the goal reached through actions. Hence, we ask you, O great sage.
107.3: How do men go to the abode of Yama through that path? O foremost among eloquent persons, tell us the magni¬ tude and extent of the path.
107.4: O omniscient sage, we earnesdy ask you to tell us entirely. O sage, how do men avert the miseries of hell?
107.5: By what means do they prevent the hellish tortures? By charitable gifts, holy rites and observances?
107.6: How do people attain the heavenly goal? By what deeds do they go to hell? How many are the abodes in heaven? How many are the hellish abodes?
107.7: How do men of good deeds go? How do men of evil deeds go? What is the form and what is the magnitude? What is the caste of the two? Even as an individual soul is being led to Yama's abode what is its form, shape and extent?
107.8: O leading sages, listen, even as I recount. O sages of good holy rites, the cycle of worldly existence is unageing. It has no permanent existence.
107.9: I shall decisively mention the path of Yama entirely. I shall recount everything in detail beginning from the time of departure. I shall recount it in a manner that no one else will be able to recount.
107.10: O excellent ones, I shall mention the form and nature of the path about which you have asked me and also the dis¬ tance between the world of Yama and the mortal world.
107.11: That pathway should of necessity be traversed by all living beings called individual souls. Meritorious men go to the meritorious sections and the sinful go to the sinful.
107.12: Those who make charitable gifts of water and cooked rice do not undergo any forture there along with their wives, sons and kins.
107.13: He who makes a charitable gift of cooked rice with the mind sanctified by faith derives satisfaction there even without (the presence of) cooked rice then.
107.14: The tlieist who lias faith in God or holy scriptures, utters no falsehood and by whom severance of affection has not been effected, attains a happy death.
107.15: These men face a happy death:—those who are devot¬ ed to the worship of Devas and brahmins, those who are not jealous, those who have spotless character, those who are liberal in gifts and those who possess the attribute of modesty.
107.16: He who does not eschew virtue either due to lust or due to fury or out of hatred; he who carries out what is men¬ tioned by elders and he who is gentle meets with a comfortable death.
107.17: Those who offer water to the thirsty, give food to the hungry, meet with timely death with ease and happiness.
107.18: He attains another body having the same shape as the previous one. It is for experiencing the tortures caused by his bad Karman. This body does not originate from the parents.
107.19: Watched by those people in distress, with their eyes full of tears he casts off his body, attains a gaseous form and goes ahead.
107.20: On seeing the living creature with the span of life extinct, the terrible emissaries of Yama come there desirous of taking him aw&y.
107.21: The emissaries of Yama are excessively terrible and competent to frighten all living beings. They assume different forms and their faces resembl.e those of bears, buffaloes, vampires.
107.22: Some have long faces; some are hideous-faced; some have crooked nooses; some have three eyes. They have massive jaw bones, cheeks and faces. Some have hanging lips.
107.23: The limbs of some are smeared with blood and flesh. Their teeth come out of their mouths resembling spouts of shooting plants. They arc very hideous in their shape. Their curved fangs are very fierce.
107.24: Their mouths resemble the nether worlds with blazing terrible tongues. The eyes are awful in their shape and size. They are shining, roving and tawny-coloured.
107.25: The eyes of some resemble fire or the eyes of the cat or owl. Some eyes are protruded like the eyes of the beetle. Some resemble the glowworm. Their hair are dishevelled and stand erect.
107.26: They are bedecked in garlands and skulls. Their limbs drip with blood (?). Their ornaments resemble terrible ser¬ pents tied up round their heads.
107.27: There are black serpents round their necks. They are very terrible due to their kissing sounds. Their tresses are coarse and stiff. They arc terrible and they resemble fiery flames.
107.28: Some of them have only two arms; others have four arms, still others have ten, sixteen or twenty arms. •
107.29: There are still others with innumrable hands. Some of them have thousand arms. Terrible weapons of various forms shine in their hands.
107.30: These emissaries of great strength threaten the aying men with different brilliant weapons such as javelin, iron club, discus etc. or nooses, fetters and batons.
107.31: When the span of life of the men comes to an end these extremely terrible emissaries come to take away the creatures. All of them carry out the orders of Yama.
107.32: The creature assumes a physical body befitting tortures in the hell and originating from its own actions. It is this body of the creature that is taken away towards the abode of Yama.
107.33: With the nooses, adamantine fetters andiron chains, the creature is bound by the infuriated servants of Yama. He is beaten and taken over to the abode of Yama.
107.34: That great path has to be traversed by these sinful per¬ sons frightened in some places, terrified in some places and faltering here and there. They are shouting and lamenting due to misery.
107.35: The living beings have to traverse the path even as they are rebuked and burnt in their bodies, They are agitated due to terror. They run about in great dejection and agitation.
107.36: Men who are devoid of charitable gifts are scorched and burnt by the heated sand. They have to go along the path strewn with thorns.
107.37: Those who are guilty of slaying living beings have to traverse the path with their bodies emitting putrescent odour of
107.38: The destroyers of living beings must of necessity go along the path shouting and lamenting, cooing and chirping out of tune. They shall be in agony due to their pain.
107.39: Those who are guilty of slaying living beings must of necessity go along the path even as they arc being pierced and smashed by javelins, iron clubs, swords, maces and arrows or by the sharp pointed tridents.

108.1: O ascetic, how do the sinners go to that city by the southern path? We wish to hear. Recount it in detail.
108.2: On seeing such a terrible doorway, those who have committed sins faint and lose consciousness suddenly. They begin to babble and prattle due to fear.
108.3: Then the servants of Yama bind them with chains and nooses and drag them ruthlessly. They beat them with sticks and threaten them again and again.
108.4: After regaining consciousness they go towards the southern door faltering at every step. They are smeared with blood.
108.5: When the extremely rough, coarse and chill wind blows against them they shrink, shrivel and become frozen.
108.6: On hearing the words ofYama's servants they lose their taste therein. They are afflicted by hunger and thirst (all the more). Thereafter they are tortured by the servants of Yama with terrible weapons.
108.7: They do not get the opportunity of either getting in or coming out. They are in a highly wretched state. Those sinners are overwhelmed by their own actions. They lament piteously.
108.8: After restraining and afflicting them much the sinners are taken by the servants of Yama to that place where Yama himself is present.
108.9: Now, when you are being afflicted by your own ac¬ tions, why do you repent and bewail? Experience your own miseries. It is not the fault of anyone else.
108.10: Due to your greed for the kingdom, due to delusion
108.11: We do not see all that strength of yours whereby the subjects have been destroyed. You are being hit and pierced by the emissaries of Yama now. Now see, what have you gained?
108.12: Touched by the wind he slowly regains life. Then they throw the man into the ocean of hellish life.
108.13: O leading brahmins, the emissaries intimate to Yama about the people engaged in sinful activities who are now extremely miserable.
108.14: This man has had sexual intercourse with forbidden women. He is a wicked man. He is a person who stole away other men's wealth. He has sold his daughter. He is a perjuror. He is ungrateful. He has deceived friends.
108.15: Virtue and piety has always been censured by this pioud follow. A sinful deed has been committed by this wicked man in the mortal world.
108.16: Now, O lord of Devas, mention the modes of restrain¬ ing or blessing this fellow. Our lord must be competent to lay down action against him. We will be only hindering if we do anything ourselves.
108.17: The tongues of those who take false pledges and speak words that wound the sensitive spots in others are plucked by the servants of Yama, who are the members of the assembly.
108.18: Those who carnally approach the daughters-in-law are hurled over the heaps of burning coal and burnt by the ser¬ vants of Yama.

109.1: Served by heavenly damsels they go the city of Dhamia- raja travelling by different divine aerial chariots rendered splendid by diamonds and gold.
109.2: Those who devoutly give the brahmins gifts of various forms go comfortably along that great path.
109.3: Those who speak truth, those who are devoid of impuri¬ ties inwardly and outwardly, go to the abode of Yama by serial chariots. They resemble the immortal beings in lustre.
109.4: Those who make gifts of gold, silver, corals or pearls, travel in aerial chariots shining like furnished gold.
109.5: Those who make gifts of houses and residences go to the abode of Dharmaraja (making use of) rest houses embel¬ lished in gold and resembling the rising sun.
109.6: Those who make gifts of water pots, different types of vessels such as Kundika, Karaka etc. go (along the path) by means of lordly elephants. They are honoured by celestial damsels too.
109.7: Those who give to brahmins oil for applying over the feet or on the head, those who give water for bath and drink unto the brahmins, go to the abode of Yama by riding on horses.
109.8: Those who accord rest to brahmins who are travel- worn and emaciated go comfortably along the path in a vehicle drawn by ruddy geese.
109.9: He who greets and honours a brahmin offering him welcome and befitting seat goes along that path comfortably. He becomes excessively delighted.
109.10: He who salutes Hari saying cc obeisance, O lord, favour¬ ably disposed to the brahmins 75 and he who salutes a cow saying "O dispeller of sins 55, goes along that path comfortably.
109.11: Those who take meals after the guests have taken and those who are devoid of arrogance and untruthfulness, go along that path by means of vehicles drawn by Sarasas (waterfowls).
109.12: Those who take only a morsel of food (each day) and are devoid of obstinacy and arrogance go to the abode of Yama comfortably by means of aerial chariots drawn by swans.
109.13: Those who have conquered the sense-organs and sustain themselves on a single morsel of food once in four days, go to the city of Dharma in vehicles drawn by peacock.
109.14: Those who regularly do virtuous deeds and take food once in three days go to that region by means of vehicles and divine chariots fitted with elephants.
109.15: He who takes cooked rice once in six days, has conquer¬ ed the sense-organs, and always maintains cleanliness, goes like the consort of SacI seated on an elephant.
109.16: (He goes to) the beautiful city of Dharmaraja em¬ bellished with jewels, resonant with different notes and voices as well as the shouts of victory.
109.17: Those who observe fasts for a forthnight go to the city of Dharmaraja in vehicles drawn by tigers and attended by Devas and Asuras.
109.18: Those who have conquered their sense-organs and observe fasts for a month go to the abode of Yama in vehicles as refulgent as the sun.
109.19: He who sanctifies the body with the inner soul devoted to Visnu goes to heaven in a chariot as refulgent as fire.
109.20: He who remembers Visnu and casts off his vital airs without resorting to destructive weapons goes to the city of Dharma by means of a vehicle that has the refulgence of the sun.
109.21: He who enters water and casts off his vital airs, goes comfortably in a vehicle resembling the lunar disc.
109.22: The devotee of Visnu who gives up his body to the vultures, goes to the abode of Yama in a splendid chariot made of gold.
109.23: He who meets death in a battle ensuing upon his at¬ tempt to resist the abduction of a woman or capture of cows goes along shining like the sun and attended upon by celestial girls.
109.24: Those devotees of Visnu who have conquered their sense-organs and undertake pilgrimages to holy centres go along that terrible path by comfortable vehicles.
109.25: The excellent brahmins who worship, performing sacri¬ fices wherein monetary gifts are generously distributed go com¬ fortably by means of aerial chariots resembling molten gold.
109.26: Those who refrain from inflicting pain on others and those who sustain their servants, go comfortably in aerial chariots shining like gold.
109.27: Those who worship Visnu, Brahma, the three-eyed lord Siva and the sun with the same emotional fervour go there immediately with a pure mind.
109.28: Those who arc devoted to truth, cleanliness and mercy and do not eat flesh go to the city of Dharmaraja comfortably.
109.29: Formerly, Brahma, the most excellent one among the knowers of the Vedas, said thus He who makes a gift of a thousand cows and he who abstains from eating meat—these two are on a par with each other.
109.30: O brahmins, the benefit resulting from the avoidance of meat-eating is the same as that of the pilgrimage to all holy centres and of the performance of all Yaj'nas.
109.31: Thus the virtuous ones engaged in charitable gifts and religious vows go comfortably in vehicles to the world of Yama the lord who is the son of the sun.
109.32: On seeing those virtuous persons lord Yama will hon¬ our them by offering them greetings of welcome, seats and pleasing water for washing feet and materials of worship.
109.33: Men who have magnificence of meritorious deeds find armaraja very gentle, as though he is their father himself.
109.34: O brahmins, if one resorts to it, virtue saves one from great dangers. One shall undoubtedly attain divinity and brahminhood by means of virtue.
109.35: O excellent brahmins, when the previously accumulated demerit of men dwindles, their mind turns to virtue.
109.36: If, after thousands of births in the other species one attains the rare birth as a human being, but still one does not practice virtue, he is a deceived persons indeed.
109.37: The following should be known as persons devoid of virtue—Despicable persons, ugly ones, impoverished men, sick men, foolish ones and those who serve others.
109.38: Virtue has been practised previously by the following persons those who live long, the heroic ones, scholars, those who have wealth, those who are free from ailments and those who are beautiful and handsome.
109.39: O brahmins, those who are engaged in righteous acti¬ vities attain the highest state. Those who resort to sin and evil are born as animals and low creatures.
109.40: Those who always bow to the lord who has neither birth nor death and who slays Daityas and Danavas, do not see Yama.
109.41: Those who have sought refuge in Visnu in their thoughts, words and deeds get the benefit of salvation. Yama is not able to harm them.
109.42: O brahmins, those people who continuously bow to Narayana, the lord of worlds, do not go anywhere else other than the abode of Visnu.
109.43: By bowing to Visnu, (the devotees) do not see those emissaries, Yama, that city or. that path. They never see hells.
109.44: Although those who are deluded may commit sins, still if they are devoted to Hari, the destroyer of sins, they do not go to hell.
109.46: Those who remember the lord even roguishly, go to the world of Visnu, free from ailments, after casting off this mortal body.
