139.10: O king, this great truth should not be imparted to a person not abiding by the Vedas. It imparts enlightenment in regard to a person who is desirous of acting according to it. It admonishes one who bows down for enlightenment.
139.11: This truth should not be imparted to a liar nor to a rogue, nor to an impotent person nor to a person of crooked intellect. It should not be imparted to a person who harasses scholars devoted to knowledge. It should be imparted for the enlightenment of the disciples. This secret should be imparted to a person who has discrimination, who is fond of injunctions, who is devoid of quarrelsome dispute, who has learned much, who has humble dress and demeanour and who has no selfish motive.
139.12: They say that knowledge of this great Brahman should not be imparted to a person who is devoid of these qualities. The narration of virtue in regard to such person is not conducive to welfare, because it is like charity accorded to a person who does not deserve it.
139.13: This should not be given to a person who has no sacred rites even if the entire earth full of jewels were given away. O leader of men, this great thing should be imparted to a per¬ son who has conquered his sense organs, who observes pure rites and who knows reality. O Karala, let there be no fear at all in you. This great Brahman has been heard by you today. It has been duly re¬ counted. It is extremely sacred. It is fully free from grief. It has neither beginning nor middle nor end.
139.14: I have been asked by you, O leader of men. So this has been recounted to you exclusively # as it had been obtained from Brahma. It is the great knowledge, the utmost resort of those who are conversant with salvation.

142.2: A common word for several types of austerities involving bathing, fas¬ ting, worship and other prescribed religious observances.
142.3: Ten thousand years before, when Devas were ascendant Taraka 1 became very powerful. He became very arrogant due to the boons granted by me.
142.4: O lord, you are the saviour of the worlds. You increase the fame of Devas. O lord of all, O source of origin of the Uni¬ verse, O lord with the three Vedas for your form,obeisance to you.
142.5: You alone are the creator of the world, destroyer of Asuras and lord of the worlds. O Jaganmaya (who are identical with the Universe), you are the cause of creation, sustenance, and destruction. You are the father and mother of the universe. O lord, you are easily accessible through service. Be pleased, O lord, save us from great dangers. Say, who is the destroyer of our distress excepting you?
142.6: You are the primordial maker. You are the Boar, Fish and Tortoise. 8 When fear overwhelms us you protect us by assu¬ ming different forms.
142.7: O lord Hari, we have no other refuge. Our lordship has been taken away. Our women have been disgraced. We have been rendered homeless. O lord, why don't you protect us? A demon who after propitiating Siva by his penance became a great terror to the world and was ultimately killed by Skanda.
142.8: The three kinds are adhyatmika, adhidaivika and adhibhautika or those due to diseases and other bodily causes, those due to super-natural agencies and those caused by natural calamities.

142.12: Pierced by the arrows the three-eyed lord may fix his mind on her. Then the lord will certainly marry her.
142.13: The arrows of the victorious Cupid have never been ineffective anywhere. So when the mother of the Universe gets married a son will be born to her. Saying "So be it" Devas, the suppressors of their enemies felt relieved. They sent Cupid and Spring to Siva.
142.14: Holding his bow and accompanied by Spring and his consort Rati, Cupid hurried to perform that very difficult task.

144.5: O lord of the worlds, O lord holding conch, discus and club, we are distressed. Your lordship always holds weapons for our sake.

145.1: How the River Ganga stationed in the water-jar reached the matted hair of Lord Siva, has been heard. Kindly tell me how* it reached the mortal world. O highly intelligent one, there are two divisions in the waters stationed in the matted hair of Mahesvara, because of two persons who took them away. For your pleasure, O dear one, I shall recount in detail how the river was brought by the brahmin or the other one.
145.2: O sage of great lustre, Ganga became the beloved of Sambhu at the very time when Uma became the beloved of the lord of Devas. Ganga alone came out of the matted hair for some other reason. Siva had concealed Ganga in his matted hair. On account of that misery Uma said "Oh, I am help¬ less."
145.3: The lord will never abandon Ganga even if attempted Wife of Pufpadanta, a gaga (attendant of Siva). Excepting his hermitage in no ocher place the offer¬ ing was made to Devas or manes. O dear son, there was neither a donor nor a Hotr 1 nor a person performing sacrifices.
145.4: Sage Gautama became well known in the world of Devas and in the mortal world. People knew that he alone was the donor and the enjoyer of pleasant things. An officiating priest reciting Rgvedic hymns during a sacrifice. On hearing about this the sages of different hermitages enquired about the hermitage of Gautama and went there.
145.5: Sage Gautama devoutly nourished all those sages as if they were his disciples, sons or fathers. After saying this to his mother, the lord of obstacles 1 went to the place where the lean Gautama who was wearing
145.6: Gautama said humbly with palms joined in reverence: Stay here alone ye all. O leading sages, I shall serve your feet. While I stand by here, ready to serve you all, it is not proper for you, Devas on the Earth to resort to another hermitage. On hearing these words of the sage, Vinayaka remem¬ bered his duty of causing obstacles (in secret). With palms joi¬ ned in reverence he said to the brahmins.
145.7: We have all been bought over by the food offered to us. Why then should Gautama not forbid us? We are not allowed to go to our own abodes by peaceful means. Nor does this excellent brahmin who has helped us deserve any punishment. Hence I shall endeavour in an intelli¬ gent manner. Let that be approved of by you all.
145.8: O Lady of splendid face, do everything in such a man¬ ner as no one else comes to know. Assume the form of a cow and go to the place where Gautama is present. Consume the paddy. O beautiful lady, destroy them and distort them. If you are beaten, or shouted at or even looked at do something (by way of retaliation). Bellowing loudly remain in a struggle between life and death. On being forbidden by him, the cow cried aloud and fell down. When the cow fell down there was a great hue and cry.
145.9: Ou hearing the cry and on seeing the action of Gautama the brahmins became distressed. Keeping Vighnaraja at the head the brahmins said. All of us are going away from here. We should not stay in your hermitage. We all had been nurtured by you like a son. O leading sage, we are taking leave of you.
145.10: On hearing these words of the brahmins who were determined to go from there, he was as though struck down by the thunderbolt. He fell down in front of the brahmins. The brahmins said to him: "See this goddess mother of the Rudras, the beloved deity of the worlds sanctifying them, fallen on the ground. When due to the power of fate, this cow whose form and features are like those of gods and holy centres has fallen down O excellent sage, what remains for us to do is to go away.
145.11: If we continue to reside in your hermitage (the merit of) the holy rites performed by us will dwindle down and waste away. O brahmin, we do not have any other asset. We are only ascetics whose only assets are their penance. This intelligent (brahmin) will speak in accordance with the opinion of all of us. His statement is (as good as) our statement. It should be considered authoritative by you, O Gautama.
145.12: Induced by the brahmins as well as the powerful Gautama, Vighnakrt (i.e. Lord GaneSa) in the guise of a brah¬ min spoke these words to all. I shall speak truthfully on behalf of all. Let the sages as well as Gautama accept my suggestion. We have heard that the water that had been in the jar of Brahma born of the unmanifest one, is now staying within the matted hair of Lord Siva.
145.13: Bring it quickly by means of austerities and holy rites. O holy sage, pour that water over this cow that has fallen on the ground. After that all of us shall stay in your house as before. When that leading brahmin said thus in the assembly of the brahmins, there was a shower of flowers there. Cries of "Victory" rose up. Then the humble Gautama spoke these words with palms joined in reverence.
145.14: Let the desire in my mind be fulfilled due to my power of penance, by the grace of Fire god, by the grace of gods and Brahma as well as by your grace. After saying "Let it be so," the brahmins took leave of the leading sage and went to their abodes that were now rich in food and water. When those brahmins had gone, Ganesvara returned accompanied by his brother and Jaya. After fulfilling his task he was extremely delighted.

146.1: After going to the peak of Kailasa what did the holy lord, Sage Gautama do? Did he perform any penance? What excellent method did he adopt for attaining the goal?
146.2: (Lord Siva) accompanied by Uma assumes eight cosmic bodies that are always beneficial to the people. It is to bestow the desired enjoyment of worldly pleasures to those who seek it that the lord assumes these bodies. Hence the people eulogize the lord as the Great God.
146.3: Ilvara assumes the body of the Earth for this purpose viz. in order to create happiness by means of its own objects of pleasure and to sustain the entire (universe consisting of) mobile and immobile beings. It is conducive to the prosperity of the universe and its increase.
146.4: The form of waters (of Siva with eight cosmic bodies) is for creation, sustenance and annihilation of the Earth and also in order to provide for support to the Earth. For granting hap¬ piness Mid piety to the people, Siva of tranquil body assumed the form of waters that is well established in the universe.
146.5: Siva'* cosmic bodies of Sun, Moon and Fire caused the following viz., the demarcation of the units of time, the oozing current of nectar, sustenance, creation and destruction of living beings and joy, happiness and progress of the subjects.
146.6: Without mutual differences there cannot be action and piety, a thing that is one's own and not one's own, neither dire¬ ctions nor atmosphere, neither heaven nor Earth, neither worldly pleasures nor salvation. Hence, O Isa, this ethereal body of yours.
146.7: (This ethereal body) assumes the form of word. In order to establish virtue the Vedas are divided into Rk, Yajus and Saman. In the world (i.e. among non-Vedic sacred litera¬ ture) the Gathas (songs), Smjrtis, Puranas etc. (also flourish).
146.8: The various ancillary objects pertaining to sacrifice constitute the sacrificial body of Siva. The sacrifice and the instruments of sacrifice, the form of the Rtvik, time, space and result, O Sambhu, you are all these things. They say that your sacrificial body is the ultimately real entity.
146.9: You are everything. You are the maker, donor, surety, charitable offering, the omniscient witness, the great Puru§a, the supreme soul and the ultimate reality. You are everything. Of what avail are the verbal outpourings?
146.10: You are not pointed out by the Vedas and other sac¬ red literature or preceptors. Nor are you accessible by means of intellect etc. You alone are unborn, unmeasurable and the lord expressed by the word Siva. You alone are the Truth. O holy lord, obeisance unto you.

147.1: After leading the Ganga from the matted hair of Mahes- vara and coming to the holy mountain Brahmagiri, what did Gautama do?
147.2: O mother born of the matted hair of the three-eyed lord, O goddess bestowing all desired things, forgive. You are calm. Go happily, carry out what is conducive to the welfare of all.
147.3: On being spoken to thus by Gautama, the Ganga who assumed a divine form and wore a divine garland and unguent, said to Gautama.
147.4: Where shall I go? To the abode of Devas, or to the water-jar or to the nether worlds? It is known that you are truthful of speech.
147.5: O goddess, you have been requested by me for helping the three worlds. You have been given to me by &ambhu. O goddess, let it not be otherwise.
147.6: Everywhere it has the power of everyone of the chan¬ nels. It destroys all sins. It bestows all desired things always. It is thus alone that she is sung about in the Vedas.
147.7: Human beings see only the part of Ganga that flows over the mortal world and not that which flows over the nether worlds. Nor do the human beings of ignorant intellect see Ganga flowing in heaven.
147.8: Then Gautama the great among the sages circumam¬ bulated Ganga, the splendid mother of the Universe fre¬ quented by Devas and Sages.

148.1: That sage said to the king, "To one of your wives a son will be born and he will sustain the family. To the other wife there will be born sixty thousand sons."
148.2: When the sage went away after bestowing the boon, thousands of sons were born. The king performed horse and other sacrifices and distributed plenty of gifts to the deserving.
148.3: In one horse sacrifice the king got himself duly initia¬ ted. He employed his sons along with their armies in the work of protecting the horse.
148.4: Getting a loophole somewhere Indra took away the horse. Those sons searched for the horse but could not find it.
148.5: Not being able to see the horse, the powerful sons of Sagara wandered here and there. Even then they did not find the horse.
148.6: They went to the world of gods then. Searching the mountains, lakes and forests, they did not see the horse then.
148.7: The holy rite for the safe journey and other similar auspicious rites were performed by the officiating priests on behalf of the king. Unable to see that beautiful creature, the king became worried.
148.8: Wandering (here and there) the sons of Sagara went to the world of Devas in their search for the horse. The horse was not there.
148.9: Thereafter the sons of the king came to the Earth and searched the mountains and forests. There also they did not see the horse then.
148.10: Distressed by hunger they went on eating dry soil day and night. They dug up hurriedly and rushed to the nether world.
148.11: On hearing that the powerful princes, the sons of Sagara who had accomplished their tasks had come (to the nether world) the asuras became frightened and they went near Kapila. 1
148.12: He had achieved that success by continuous wofk without any sleep. Therefore he was tired. When the task had been accomplished the glorious Kapila said to Devas, "Give me a place for sleeping."
148.13: Then the sons of Sagara entered the nether regions. They saw the tethered horse and the man lying down.
148.14: A celebrated sage and propounder of the Sarfikhya system of philosophy. He is said Jto be the son of Karandama-Prajapati and Devahuti. The Brah- magdapuraa (ch. 93) mentions him as an incarnation of Vijpu.
148.15: Then Kapila the excellent sage stared at the sons of Sagara with great fury. With his anger he reduced them to ashes.
148.16: Then all the sons of Sagara were burnt up. But the king Sagara who was initiated to the sacrifice did not know these things.
148.17: On hearing those words of Sagara, the ministers hur¬ riedly abandoned the son of the king. Asamafijas went to the forest.
148.18: Propitiating Kapila, the boy Am&iman gave the horse to Sagara. Thus was the sacrifice completed.
148.19: On hearing about the sad end of all of his grandfathers he became very distressed. The humble prince asked the great king,
148.20: "How shall I accomplish the expiation of the Sagaras?" The king said to Bhagiratha, "Dear son, Kapila knows it".
148.21: On hearing his words the boy went to the nether world. After bowing down to the sage, he intimated everything to him.
148.22: On hearing the words of the sage that boy whose acti¬ vities were those of children bowed down to the sage and went to the mountain Kailasa. Becoming pure (in mind and body) he decided to perform penance. (Then) Bhagiratha said:
148.23: O lord, wearing crescent moon, I am a boy and my intellect too is puerile. I do not know anything. Even then, be pleased, O lord.
148.24: May Siva bring about things desired by those by whom I have been begot and nurtured, those whose Gotra (lineage) is the same as mine and those whose duties are also the same. I bow down to lord Siva with the crescent moon on his head.

148.26: O goddess, my ancestors have fallen as a result of the curse of sage Kapila. O mother, it behoves you to save them therefrom.
148.27: A class of inferior deities who, according to Vi$nupurapa, were the grandchildren of Dak$a-Prajapati.

150.1: I am not competent to recount to you the greatness of Kusavarta. Merely by remembering it one's purpose is accom¬ plished. The sage brought the river after stirring it with Kusa. Performing ablution and offering charitable gifts there bestows satisfaction to the manes.
150.2: A sacred" grass used in religious rites; also known as darbha in older texts. That sinner killed animals and birds of many forms. Some of them, both living and dead, he put inside a cage.
150.3: He returned home scorched and distressed due to hunger and thirst after wandering through many places. He thought of his wife and children wondering whether they were alive or not. In the meantime the sun also set.
150.4: He lived there happily well-contented, delighted and free from fear. Many years passed by since that bird began to live there. "Even now my beloved wife, the source of my welfare, who increases my joy, the mother of my virtue and the control¬ ling mistress of my body, has not come back.
150.5: ~She is a comrade unto me; she helps me by her counsels. She abides by my words and suggestions. Even after the sun has She does not know any holy rite, mantra, god, virtue or asset other than me, her husband. Her husband is her holy rite; her husband is her life; her husband is her Mantra. She is fond of her husband.
150.6: Even now my beloved, the source of my welfare has not come back. What shall I do? Where shall I go? Is this my house? Without her it appears to be a forest. O bird of great intellect, I am here imprisoned (and) helpless. I have been brought here by the hunter bound by ropes and nooses.
150.7: You are my deity. You are my lord. You are my friend. You are my ultimate resort. You are my holy rite. You are the great Brahman. You are my heaven. You are my salvation.
150.8: O my beloved husband, the cause of my welfare, do not be worried. Make your intellect steady and stable in virtue and piety. It is by your favour that different kinds of worldly pleasu¬ res have been enjoyed by me. Do not have any grief or worry due to me. Keep your intellect steady and stable in virtue and piety.
150.9: On hearing these words of his beloved the he-pigeon got
150.10: On approaching, he saw his beloved, and the hunter as though dead. He said, "Now the hunter is motionless. I shall release you." If his feet are washed the manes are pleased. If he is given food to eat, Prajapati is pleased. By rendering service to him Laksiru can be propitiated along with Vi?nu.
150.11: O lady of excellent face, what has been said by you is
150.12: There are some who fill their belly with thousands; others with hundreds and still others with tens. Some fill them¬ selves with happiness. But we fill our belly with great difficulty. Some hoard their wealth and grain in deep pits. Others hoard their wealth in big barns. Some keep their wealth in pots. But we keep our wealth in our beaks.
150.13: O splendid lady, how shall I honour and propitiate this exhausted guest?
150.14: Fire, water, splendid speech etc., can be offered to the guest. Grass, wood etc. should also be given to the suppliant. This hunter is distressed due to chillnes». On hearing these words of his beloved the king of birds ascended the tree and saw a fire burning far off.
150.15: During the mid-night he dropped dry twigs, leaves and grass into that fire.
150.16: On seeing the fire blazing, that hunter who was distressed by cold warmed his exhausted limbs and attained happiness. On seeing the hunter consumed by the fire of hunger, the she-pigeon said to her husband, "O highly fortunate one, release me.
150.17: I shall propitiate the distressed hunter with my own body. O dear one of good holy rites, attain the worlds belonging to those who have worshipped their guests".
150.18: O splendid lady, when I stand (i.e. when I am alive) this duty is not laid down for you. I shall be the one who pro¬ pitiates the guest, permit me to be so. Fie upon this life of mine with a human body, for, this daring act has been undertaken for my sake by this king of birds.
150.19: On hearing her words the hunter released the she-pigeon from the cage hurriedly as though he was afraid.
150.20: The woman who follows her husband shall stay in hea¬ ven for as many years as there are hairs on a man's body, viz. three and a half crores of years. After saying thus, the good mannered she-bird entered the fire. As soon as she entered the fire there was a cry of victory.
150.21: Then the pair were seen in the sky seated on an aerial chariot resembling the sun and extremely splendid. They were like gods themselves.
150.22: O highly fortunate ones, I am not to be abandoned by you. Something should be given to me who do not know any¬ thing. I am your guest here and thus should be honoured. It behoves you to recount to me the manner of my expiation. Go to Gautami river, welfare be to you. Taking bath there for a fortnight you will be liberated from your sins.
150.23: After being liberated from your sins if you plunge into Ganga again you will acquire the merit of a horse-sacrifice. You will become sanctified.

153.1: O great sage, listen to the description of the holy centre of Dasasvamedha 1. Merely by listening to its name one shall acquire the merit of a horse-sacrifice.
153.2: "O sage, I wish to perform a horse sacrifice simultaneously with ten horses."
153.3: He said: "O excellent king, there are Devayajanas (places for the worship of Devas) at different places where ex¬ cellent brahmins performed great sacrifices."
153.4: Ten sacrifices were simultaneously performed by the priest. In that sacrifice in a group, a number of sages were employed as Rtviks.
153.5: A sacred place in Kurukyetra (MBh, Vanaparva, 9.14)
153.6: Is it because of the defect of place, or of the defect of time, or my defect or your defect that the ten horse sacrifices have not become complete?
153.7: The grief-stricken king accompanied by his preceptor KaSyapa went to Samvarta the elder brother of Brhaspati. They spoke to him.
153.8: O holy sage, the bestower of honour, ten horse-sacrifices have to be performed simultaneously. Tell us about the place and the preceptor thereof so that all the ten will be completed.
153.9: The excellent sage Samvarta meditated for a while and spoke to Bhauvana: "Go to Brahma. He will tell you about the preceptor and the place of sacrifice."
153.10: Bhauvana of great intellect came to me accompanied by the noble Kasyapa. They asked me about the preceptor, place of sacrifice and other things.
153.11: Then O dear son, I spoke to Bhauvana and Kasyapa: "O leading king, go to Gautami. That place is highly merito¬ rious for sacrifices.
153.12: On hearing it the king Bhauvana went to the banks of Gautami with Kasyapa to assist him. He got himself initiated for the horse sacrifice.
153.13: Lit. lord of the seat or sacrificial assembly. Both of them, viz. Anjana and Adrika worshipped the excellent sage Agastya duly and pleasingly.
153.14: Then the delighted holy sage said to them, "Let a boon be chosen". They said to Agastya, "O lord of sages, give us two sons.
153.15: They should be stronger than all others and more excel¬ lent too. They should be persons who render help to the whole world". "By taking bath in Gautami you will be released from the curse". After saying this the two delighted Devas vanished there itself.
153.16: Then, for the sake of pleasing his brother Hanuman, Adri who had the form and features of a Pisaca took Afijana, his mother and made her take her bath.

162.1: Unable to see anyone to protect her, that beautiful widow with a young son went to the hermitage of Galava.
162.2: After entrusting her son to him that woman deluded by sin wandered here and there over many countries leading a lec¬ herous life.
162.3: Although their union lasted for a long time, the mother and the son did not know the real facts about each other.
162.4: Although the brahmin's actions were bad, he possessed a good mind due to the virtue of his father. Listen to this wonder¬ ful account, O Narada.
162.5: Living a carefree life he did not abandon prayers per¬ taining to Brahman. After performing the morning prayers he worked for earning wealth.
162.6: Who are you? Where will you go? What do you do? Where do you eat? What is your name? Where do you sleep? Who is your wife? Tell me.
162.7: By virtue of the sanctity of this Tirtha, due to the grace of this goddess, you have been purified, O dear one, everyday. In this matter you need not worry at all.

163.1: They know this as Pitjtlrtha, O brahmin, because it was the place where Rama, the son of DaSaratha, propitiated his ancestors, in the company ofSita.
163.2: If holy bath, charitable gift and water libation unto the ancestors were performed there everything attains an everlasting status. No worry need be felt in this respect.
163.3: Let something to eat, something to munch and crunch be brought, no matter what the quantity be, in whatever manner possible, from wherever it is available. Let it be brought as it is. Do not delay. You must go now itself. It must be brought in a trice.
163.4: Indra in the form of a bird, thereupon, placed the pot filled with honey among the comets. ViSvamitra became angry. On seeing the pot, the sage said thus furiously.
163.5: "Give us the dog's flesh alone. You can take away the excellent nectar. If not, I shall reduce you to ashes."
163.6: "Perform the Homa of honey duly and drink it along with your sons. Of what avail is this unholy filthy flesh of a dog, O great sage?"

164.1: The holy centre known as Sveta Tirtha in the three worlds is very auspicious. On being simply remembered it rids people of all sins.
164.2: O Mrtyu, why does not Sveta come yet? His span of life has come to an end. Nor have the messengers of Mrtyu too come yet. Why? This pazzles me.
164.3: The infuriated Mrtyu thereupon went himself to the abode of Sveta. Seeing his messengers highly frightened and standing mum, Mrtyu said, "What is the matter, O messengers?"
164.4: Karttikeya pierced the servants of Yama by means of his javelin. He killed Yama, the powerful ruler of the southern quarter.
164.5: Even as they were eulogizing him lord Siva appeared in front of them. He asked them pleasantly: "What shall I give you?"
164.6: Then the lord said, "Certainly I shall revive him; undoubtedly I shall make Yama come back to life, if Devas agree to my suggestion now."
164.7: Then Devas said: "We shall do as you bid—you in whose control the entire Universe along with Hari, Brahma and others function."

165.4: O preceptor, everyday you teach me with discrimination.
165.6: Only teachers of deluded thinking practise discrimina¬ tion. There is no limit to the sins incurred by the persons of discriminatory feelings.
165.7: O preceptor, you have been well-understood. I shall bow down to you again and again. I shall go to another pre¬ ceptor. It behoves you to permit me.

165.13: Remaining pure in mind and body on the Gautami Tirtha propitiate Siva by means of hymns. Being pleased there¬ by the lord of three worlds will impart learning to you.

170.1: There are two holy centres viz. Suparnasahgama and Kadrava Sarigama where lord Mahesvara has resorted to the banks of Ganga.
170.2: The following holy puddles and deep pits are also there viz. Agnikun<ja, Raudra, Vaisnava, Saura, Saumya, Brahma, Kaumara and Varuna.
170.3: The river Apsara joins Ganga and that confluence is a holy centre. Merely by remembering that holy centre a man can be assured and become contented.
170.4: It quells all sins. Listen, O Narada, attentively.
170.5: Beget a splendid son through whom Indra's arrogance can be quelled. We shall give you a moiety of our penance.
170.6: That Prajapati made Suparna pregnant. He made Kadru the mother of Nagas too pregnant.
170.7: Saying, "So be it" Kasyapa of holy rites took bath in Ganga and eulogized Mahesvara, the lord of Devas, by means of sacred hymns.
170.8: You alone are competent to dispel the misery of all embodied beings, whether mobile or immobile, who have been scorched by the sun of therefold misery 1 and who run about here and there.
170.9: The three types of Yoga (contact) of Sattva etc. (Sattva, Rajas and Tamas) of Lord Siva cannot be recounted even by Sakra and others. Considering Soma (i.e. Siva) to be of diverse wonderful activities, an excellent person who is always devoted to charitable gifts is happy always.

174.1: The whole world undergoes sufferings for the sake of a son. What is it that one gets from a son? A son may be wise or foolish, excellent or middling.
174.2: Without a son, O leading king, heaven and salvation are very difficult to achieve. In the world, it is the son who is the most conducive to the achievement of virtue, love and wealth.
174.3: Tell me how I can obtain a son. I am willing to go anywhere and perform any rite, whatever be the means thereof. By manly endeavour, repetition of Mantras, performance of sacrifices or distribution of charitable gifts a son should be got by me.
174.4: The three well known debts are: (1) Rsi-rna or debt to the sages, which one discharges by the study of Veda; (2) Deva-fna or debt to the gods, which is discharged by performing worship and sacrifice; and (3) Pitr-rna or debt to the manes, which is discharged by procreation of a son. Evidently these great debts or obligations aim respectively at acquisition, dissemination and advancement of knowledge, preservation of religious and moral values, and perpetuation of the human race.
174.5: Resoiting to the banks of Gautami he propitiated Varuna. Varuna who was pleased said to Hariscandra:
174.6: O king, I shall grant you a son. Being issueless you have performed holy rites; certainly a son will be born to you if you are prepared to offer him in sacrifice.
174.7: If a Ksatriya happens to be the sacrificial animal, the same will be the most excellent one, if he knows the science of archery.
174.8: The king said, ' 'yes' '. After saying so, the king said to the Rtviks and his eldest son Rohita, within the hearing of Varuna:
174.9: I am pure. I am in a hurry. At the very outset, O great
174.10: O Ajigarta of great intelligence, what will you take from me? Tell me truthfully. You need not say anything else. Indeed, brahmins are truthful in speech.
174.11: Take one of the three sons, or me, or take this (woman) my wife. We shall keep alive by this sale.
174.12: O Rohita, I will not sell my eldest son Sunahpuccha. The mother will not sell the youngest one. Hence I shall sell Sunahsepa, the one between these two. Tell me the amount (you wish to give) for him.
174.13: A sacrificial animal has to be kept ready for Varuna. (He must be) a man of superior qualities. If you are willing to take a price in exchange, tell me truthfully, O great sage.
174.14: Saying "So be it" Ajigarta fixed a thousand cows, (measures) of grains, gold coins and clothes as the price of his son. "O Prince", he said, "give the excellent things (tome), I shall give my son to you".
174.15: Saying "So be it" Rohita too gave him money and clothes. After giving it, Rohita went to his father along with the son of the sage. He informed his father about the son of the sage bought for a price.

175.1: Formerly Soma (Moon) full of nectar had been the king of Gandharvas and not of Devas. Then Devas approached me and said:
175.2: Formerly Soma, the bestower of vital airs on Devas, had been taken away by Gandharvas. Not able to meditate on him, sages and Devas became extremely distressed. Let some strategic means be employed so that Soma can be ours.
175.3: Vak (Sarasvatl) said to Devas: "The Gandharvas are madly passionate over women. O Devas, it behoves you to bring Soma after giving me to them."
175.4: The immortal ones replied to Vak: "We are not com¬ petent to give you away. It is impossible to live without Soma, nor is it possible to live without you".
175.5: At the instance of Indra those Gandharvas, passionate over women, gave Soma to Devas and took Sarasvatl.

176.1: They went to the mountain Meru. Devas and Danavas consulted one another. They wished for the welfare of each other.
176.2: What has happened to the contrary should never be remembered. The pleasure that one derives from absence of enmity is not obtained even by our rule over the three worlds or by acquiring a higher position or even in salvation.
176.3: Therefrom the holy nectar dear to Devas came out. When the holy nectar was produced they said to one another:
176.4: Our enemies, our suppressors have gone after confiding in us. The nectar should not at all be given to them.
176.5: He assumed the form of Deva and held the drinking bowl. On realising that it was a Daitya, the Sun-god intimated to Soma.
176.6: Soma gave nectar to that Daitya who had the form of a non-Daitya but informed Visnu.
176.7: By means of his discus, Visnu lifted the Daitya who could manage to gulp nectar. Visnu cut off his head immediately. But, O dear one, that head became immortal.

177.1: Gautama did not engage himself in a regular study of any scriptures. But he observed vows regularly and performed rites in sacred fires.
177.2: During the course of his wanderings, Gautama came to Himalayas. There he espied a beautiful cave overgrown with creepers and branches of trees.
177.3: The great brahmin sat down there and decided to stay. Entering within he saw an excellent woman.
177.4: On seeing her the excellent sage stood ready for making obeisance to her but she prevented him.
177.5: You are about to become my Guru (preceptor). It does not behove you to salute me. Longevity, learning, wealth, fame, virtue, heavenly enjoyment etc. of a person, perish if a Guru were to bow down to his disciple*
177.6: O gentle lady, I am aged a thousand years. You are older than I. I am a boy. You are an old lady. Hence, our mutual union is impossible.
177.7: After saying this to Gautama the old lady pleaded (fire god) and made him handsome as well as learned.
177.8: Thereafter, Gautama who became learned, handsome and brilliant married the old lady. With great pleasure he sported with that charming lady for many years in the cave. He was happy and delighted in his mind.
177.9: Is this your son or grandson, old lady? Who is this Gautama? Tell us the truth, O gentle lady.
177.10: Lord of Lak§mi (i.e. Visnu) has been worshipped very well by you in your previous birth with devotion. Good charit¬ able gifts have been distributed, sacrifices with good monetary gifts have been performed (by you.)
177.11: Holy centres have been duly visited and plenty of gifts have been given and much has been sacrificed. Hence Gautama, the knower of the Vedas has been obtained by you as son.
177.12: (Defective Verse) Is he your great-grandson, grandson or son? Or is he your daughter's son? Sesainum seeds are causes of satisfaction through a son but in the case of daughter's son they are like those kept in a leather bag.
177.13: Thus spoke some of them even as the couple were lis¬ tening to their talk.
177.14: On hearing the talk of the sages the couple were ashamed and sorry. The highly intelligent Gautama in the company of his wife asked Agastya the great excellent sage:
177.15: Like a tree unto the travellers in the desert, O Siva, you in the company of your consort are the sole refuge unto those persons who are distressed in this world.
177.16: You entirely remove the sins of all living beings—high and low. O Kr§na, you are like the cloud to the planets that wither due to drought.
177.17: O GautamI, you are the ladder leading to the fort of Vaikuntha that is difficult of access. You are the river of nectar. Be the refuge of seven (? worlds) coming beneath.
177.18: Then the delighted GautamI, worthy of being sought refuge in, spoke to Gautama who was accompanied by the old woman, who had sought refuge in her and who was in great distress.
177.19: At the instance of Ganga they said 'yes' and did as they were told. Both of them obtained beautiful form by the grace of GautamI.
177.20: The water used for pouring became a river; it became well known, O excellent sage, by the name of the old woman.
177.21: "Let it be so", said Ganga to the old lady, the beloved wife of Gautama. The Linga installed by Gautama is glorified by the name Vrddha.

178.1: Once a ruler of men named Ila born of the family of Vivasvan (Sun) went to the hunting forest along with a large army.
178.2: He wandered over the forest infested with beasts of prey, full of birds of various shapes and sizes and rendered beautiful by the branches of trees.
178.3: Wandering over the forest with his mind inclined to the sport of hunting the excellent king determined to stay there. Ila said to his ministers:
178.4: All of you go to the city looked after and protected by my son. May you all look after the welfare of the land, treasury, army, kingdom as well as the Prince.
178.5: O beloved, how will I conquer (this king) who is strong, invincible, proud on account of glory and heroism, blind due to arrogance and very much attached to the sport of hunting?

179.1: The holy centre famous as Cakratlrtha destroys sins of brahmin-slaughter etc. because it was here that lord Hari ob¬ tained <his discus.
179.2: That sacrifice sponsored by Brahma and Devas was entirely surrounded by them. It had been guarded with purity of mind by Dak$a, the sacrifices
179.3: It had been looked after from all round by Vasistha and other formidable sages. It had been well protected every¬ where by Indra, Adityas, Vasus and others.
179.4: These utterances were heard all round, viz. "Let this be given," "Let this be eaten"; "Let this be done", "Stay here happily". Thus the sacrifice of Dak$a had been honoured.
179.5: After uprooting the teeth of Pu§an Vlrabhadra routed Indra in a trice. O brahmin, he pierced and split the eyes of Bhaga.
179.6: Again, he whirled the Sun-god with his arms and hurled him down. Thereupon, all Devas sought refuge in Visnu.
179.7: Save us, save us, O lord with the club in hands, from the danger arising from the leader of the Bhutas. There is a certain Gana (attendant) of Mahesvara. He is the leader of Pramathas. Even as Hari was watching the entire sacrifice pertaining to Vignu the entire sacrifice was destroyed.
179.8: In order to kill the leader of Bhutas the discus was dis charged by Hari. As it advanced and approached him the leader of Bhutas grasped it.
179.9: As he eulogized thus, Mahesvara became pleased with him and said to him, "What shall I give you"? (He replied) "O lord, let my sacrifice be complete".
179.10: "So be it" said Mahesvara, lord of Devas, Sankara, the soul of all living beings and the ocean of mercy.
179.11: After making the sacrifice of Daksa complete, O sage, and after saying thus the lord vanished along with his Bhutas.
179.12: Thereupon the lord holding the conch, discus and club became pleased and said to them: ''What for have all of you come? I shall do it for you."
179.13: O slayer of Madhu, Devas have an excessive danger from Daityas. Hence, O Lord, try to save them.
179.14: Then, after Devas had gone Vi§nu prepared himself to get the discus. After going to Godavari he began the worship of &ambhu.
179.15: With great devotion Visnu performed the daily worship of the consort of Uma with a thousand divine sweet smelling golden lotuses.
179.16: "Obeisance, the Pinaka-bearing Mahes'a, who removes great danger in the forest of worldly existence and who fulfils all cherished desires".
179.17: By means of this Mantra and with the mind endowed with devotion lord Visnu worshipped Siva, the lover of Bhavani.
179.18: O lord, you alone know the innermost feelings of men. You alone are refuge and overlord. What doubt can be there?
179.19: Speaking thus with tears welled up in his eyes he got himself merged as though with I svara. Then Sambhu appeared in front of him, accompanied by Bhavani.
179.20: He embraced Hari closely and filled him with various boons. He got back his original eye as well as discus.

180.1: Things such as water, honey etc. offered to deities, guest etc. as a token of respect. With great delight, Dadhici welcomed and honoured Devas severally. Accompanied by his wife he thereafter per¬ formed the duties of a householder to them.
180.2: We are happy, O brahmin, and especially so since we see you here. We have no use for our weapons. Indeed, we are not capable of carrying them.
180.3: The divine wish-fulfilling tree obtained by the churning of the ocean (Vide Agnipurana, Gh. 3). A long time elapsed. A thousand years according to the reckoning of Devas passed away. Devas neither spoke
180.4: Dadhlci said to Gabhasti: "O gentle lady, Asuras are powerful, behaving inimically toward me. Devas do not appear to be desirous of taking away their weapons deposited with us. Tell me what is proper in the circumstances."
180.5: She said to her husband humbly: "It has already been said, dear lord. You know what is proper in this situation. The powerful Daityas, who have increased their efficiency and who are endowed with the power of penance will take away these weapons'*. Therefore, Dadhlci did thus for protecting weapons. He washed those weapons with holy water inspired with Mantras. The water absoxbed the essential splendour of all the weapons and Dadhlci drank this holy water.
180.6: Deprived of their intrinsic splendour those weapons gradually wasted away as time passed by.
180.7: "O leading sage, give us the weapons. Can you say'Yes' or do you refuse? Without them we will be lost for ever. Our enemies are powerful. Where shall we go? Neither in the mortal world, nor in the netherworld, nor in the heaven, O dear one, is it possible for us to stay today. You are an excellent brahmin. Moreover, you are en¬ dowed with (the power of) penance. It is not proper to say anything else in your presence."
180.8: The brahmin said then: "You may take the weapons assimilated in my bones. There is no doubt about this."
180.9: Again, the excellent sage said: "I shall abandon the spirits animating my body (as) I am endowed with the power of Yoga. You may make weapons out of my bones (as they have merged with them). Let them be excellent ones with excellent forms." "Do so", said Devas in reply to Dadhici who resembled Fire-god and who was never deficient in intrinsic power. At that time the wife of the sage was not there in the vicinity to say pleasing words to him, O great sage.
180.10: On observing that his physical body had become life¬ less Devas in their hurry, said to Tvastr, "Make a number of weapons immediately".
180.11: O bullocks, to facilitate your work your faces are made adamantine in a trice by Devas for getting weapons. Tear off the body of Dadhici and give the pure bones now. At the instance of Devas they did so. They licked the bones clean and gave them to Devas. Devas of brave valour and strength hurriedly went to their abodes and so did the bullocks.
180.12: On her way, her necklace slipped from her neck and fell on the ground. The bangle also fell down from her wrist. Her right eye throbbed. Seeing all these omens she became distressed in her mind.
180.13: Those who view and protect a boy bereft of his mother and father without any distinction from their own children are certainly to be honoured and saluted even by Brahma and others. The trees in the hermitage and the residents of the forest who had been nurtured by the sage Dadhlci like his own children, began to cry.
180.14: The animals, the birds and the trees, all of them said to one another. "We cannot live without him. Nor can we live without that mother*'.
180.15: After saying thus the medicinal herbs, plants and trees approached king Soma (i.e. the Moon) and requested for excel¬ lent nectar. Soma gave them excellent nectar. They gave the boy the nectar that is dear to Devas.
180.16: Satisfied with this, the boy grew up like the moon in the bright half of the lunar month. Since he had been brought up by the Pippalas (fruits of the fig tree), the boy was (called) Pippalada (the eater of Pippala fruits). After growing up he said to the Pippalas thus in great wonder.
180.17: Men are born of men. Birds are born of birds. Plants and creepers are produced from seeds. No inconsistency is seen. How was I with hands, feet, vital breath etc. born of you? The trees took that boy to the presence of the Moon. Those trees intimated the utterance of the boy to Soma (Moon). On hearing it, Soma spoke to Pippalada:
180.18: Learn all the branches of knowledge in a formal way, my dear soil. You will attain at my behest the power of penance, auspicious speech, heroism, handsome features, strength and intellect.
180.19: After meditating for a long time the Moon said: "Whe¬ ther it is enjoyment of worldly pleasures or attainment of salva¬ tion, everything is attained undoubtedly from lord MaheSvara". He said to the Moon again: "How will I see Mahe- 3vara? I am a boy with childish intelligence. I have neither skill nor power of penance."
180.20: O lord, after hearing in detail the death of both of them on account of Devas, I am overwhelmed by misery and anger. I am not eager to live.
180.21: Hence, grant me sufficient capacity to destroy Devas. In all the three worlds, you alone, O Moon-crested one, are worthy of being served by those who should not be killed. O sinless one, if you are capable of looking at my third eye you will be competent to assail your foes.
180.22: Then he desired to look at the third eye of the lord but could not. Then he said to Sankara: "I am not able'*.
180.23: O boy, do some penance so that you will be able to look at my third eye. Then you will undoubtedly attain your desire. On hearing that aerial voice, Pippalada became angry. When the fire of pride and prestige burns within, advice regarding proper conduct is meaningless.
180.24: O Krtya, do not seize living beings remaining within a range of a Yojana (12 km) at my behest. Go far away from that place and do your duty.
180.25: That Krtya which had the form of Varava stood at a distance of a Yojana to the East from the holy centre Pippala. O Sambhu, protect us. The Krtya and the fire born of it assail us. O lord of all, O bestower of protection from fear to the frightened persons, be our refuge.
180.26: O Siva, you alone are the refuge to the creatures that are attacked from all sides, that are distressed and that are extremely wearied.
180.27: The Krtya coming from the fire of your eye has been requested by the sage and she is desirous of destroying the three worlds. You are our protector and none else. Again, they said to the lord of Devas: "O lord honoured and worshipped by gods, how shall we live here after abandoning heaven granted by you?*'
180.28: A person who has gone to heaven lives in the other world without any malady for as many years as there are days when the fascinating fame prevails in human world.
180.29: Only those who have no fame are considered dead here. Only those who are devoid of renown are (considered) blind. Those who are not habitually liberal in gifts are eunuchs. Only those who are not invariably virtuous are to be pitied. On hearing the lord of Devas the sage became calm. After bowing down to the lord he spoke with palms joined in reverence.
180.30: In the presence of the thousand-eyed lord (Indra) and others he spoke these words of fine sentiment and good syllables. Devas too agreed to the words uttered by the son of Dadhlci.
180.31: After appreciating the intellect, humility, learning, heroism, strength, truthfulness, filial devotion, and purity of emotions, Sankara said to Pippalada. Dear boy, whatever cherished desire you have and whatever is pleasing to Devas you will attain. Speak out what is conducive to your welfare. Do not hesitate to speak out your mind.
180.32: Those who take holy plunge in Ganga and those who are virtuous, O Mahesa, and sec thy lotus-like feet—let them attain their desires immediately. After their death let them attain the region ofSiva.
180.33: O lord, my father has attained your region. So also my mother, the Pippala and the immortal ones. After seeing the lord of lords they have attained happiness. Let them see you. Let them attain your region. Saying "so be it" to Pippalada, Mahesvara, lord of Devas spoke to him congratulating him along with Devas.
180.34: Devas were pleased after being freed from fear aris¬ ing from him. All of them spoke this to the son of Dadhici in the presence of Siva.
180.35: Devas repeated the same.thing to the excellent brahmin again and again. After bowing down to Sambhu, the Pippalas and Uma, Pippaiada spoke with palms joined in reverence. On seeing his parents he bowed down to them in the presence of Siva. Their eyes were filled with tears of pleasure. Somehow he spoke to them.
180.36: Other sons who perpetuate their families redeem their parents. But I am merely the cause of splitting the belly of my mother. Even though I am like this I shall look at them due to delusion. I am a wicked person with an evil mind.
180.37: On looking at them he could not speak anything further out of sorrow. Devas spoke to Pippalada and his parents. Blessed are you, dear son, whose fame has spread in the world and has gone up to heaven. The three-eyed lord has been directly perceived by you. Devas have been consoled by you. With you as son the excellent worlds will never dwindle down.
180.38: At that time a shower of flowers fell on his head from heaven. The shouts of "Victory" uttered by Devas arose, O great sage.
180.39: After bestowing blessings on his son and after bowing down to Sambhu, Ganga and Devas along with his wife Dadhlci spoke to his son. Get yourself a wife. Have devotion to Siva and serve Ganga. After procreating sons and after performing sacrifices with due gifts, dear son, you can be contented. Thereafter, proceed to heaven for a long stay there.
180.40: The place where the bones of that brahmin became sacred, O Narada, should be known as Pitrtirtha. It is condu¬ cive to the increase of delight of the manes.
180.41: Taking leave of Pippalada Devas went to their own abode. The Pippalas attained the everlasting (pleasures of) heaven after the lapse of some time. The brahmin Pippalada of great exploits established the position of trees in the overlordship of the field and wor¬ shipped Sankara.
180.42: The courageous son of Dadhlci of fierce splendour married the daughter of Gautama and begot sons. He earned wealth and fame and attained heaven along with his friends.

181.1: The holy centre well known by the name of Nagatirtha is auspicious. It bestows all cherished things. Here the lord is Nagesvara. Listen to the detailed description of the same.
181.2: In the company of his beloved wife he made great efforts for getting a son. After a long time a serpent of very terrible features was born as his son.
181.3: Surasena, the king, nursed and brought him up. No man ever knew that the king's son was a serpent.
181.4: Excepting his mother and father, no one whthin or without knew (this secret). Neither the nurse nor the chief minister nor the priest knew it.
181.5: On seeing that terrible serpent the excellent king and his wife were acutely distressed everyday. (They thought) that having no sons is far better than having a serpent for a son.

182.1: Then, along with Devas, I approached the Trident¬ armed lord standing in his abode. With my palms joined in reverence I eulogized him by reciting a number of prayers.
182.2: On being requested thus he went at the very same moment to the place where the enemies of Devas were camping. A fierce battle raged between Sankara and the enemies of Devas.
182.3: Then the three-eyed lord became tired. Siva (then) assumed the Tamasa form. As he fought, drops of sweat fell from his forehead.
182.4: Having resorted to the Tamasa form he killed Asuras. On seeing that form the Asuras went to the Earth 'from the top of Meru.
182.5: Killing all Daityas Hara too went to the Earth. Being, frightened, they went around here and there all over the Earth.
182.6: In the same manner Rudra too followed them in anger. In the same manner (as before) drops of perspiration fell down as Sambhu fought.
182.7: Wherever the drops of perspiration came into contact with the Earth, O sage, the Mothers with the features of Siva were born.
182.8: All of them said to Mahesvara, "We shall devour Asuras'*. Then the lord surrounded by Devas said:

184.1: The holy centre Avighna has been declared to be des¬ tructive of all obstacles. In this connection I shall narrate an incident. Listen devoutly, O Narada.
184.2: On the northern bank of Gautami a divine sacrifice was held but it could not be concluded due to some obstacles.
184.3: Then Devas spoke to Hari and me. Thereupon, I entered in meditation, saw the cause and spoke to them:
184.4: "This sacrifice is not concluded on account of certain obstacles created by Vinayaka. Hence, let Devas eulogize the primordial lord Vinayaka."
184.5: After saying "So be it" Devas took their holy plunge in Gautami. On the banks of the river Devas eulogized Ganesvara, the primordial lord.
184.6: May that VighneSvara, son of Ambika, bestow upon us freedom from obstacles immediately, in this great sacrifice. If he is meditated upon, the heart wishes of all embodied beings become fulfilled.

186.1: Therefore, heaven became void and the mortal world was overcrowded because they were neglected by Mrtyu. Then Devas said to the Raksasas.
186.2: *'All of you go to sacrifice. Destroy that great sacrifice of sages."
186.3: "We shall destroy that sacrifice. But what is our benefit therefrom? No one engages himself in any activity anywhere on any occasion without a proper reason."
186.4: Devas said to Asuras: "You too will get the benefit of sacrifice (?). Hence you go to the excellent sacrifice of sages".
186.5: On hearing it they hurried to the place where the sacri¬ fice was on in order to destroy it, especially at the instance of Devas.
186.6: On coming to know of it, the sages said to Mrtyu: "What shall we do? At the instance of Devas the Raksasas have come here as the destroyers of sacrifice."
186.7: After taking their holy plunge there they eulogized Mahesana for their protection. With their palms joined in reverence they eulogized the lord of Devas.
186.8: O lord of Devas, a terrible danger has befallen us from the Raksasas. Protect our sacrifice. Protect us so that our sacrifice be concluded.
186.9: The lord did so. The three-eyed bull-bannered lord did so. With Mptyu as the slaughterer the sacrifice was con¬ cluded.
186.10: The immortal ones slowly came there for their respec¬ tive shares in Havi offering. The furious sages said to them along with Mrtyu.
186.11: Since Raksasas had been sent by you for destroying our sacrifice, let the sinful Raksasas be your enemies.
186.12: A demoness or evil spirit created by black magic or bom of sacrifice for destructive purposes.

187.1: The holy centre known as Atmatirtha yields worldly pleasures and salvation to men. I shall describe the efficacy of that holy centre where Siva is called JiianeSvara.
187.2: O overlord of Devas! As ill luck would have it, I have fallen into the well of worldly existence. I am sunk in the mire of misery by delusion. I am enveloped by the darkness of ignor¬ ance. I am not able to realize the supreme soul.
187.3: I am pierced by the powerful trident of sins. I am torn asunder by the razor of worries and anxieties. I am scorched by the terrible heat of five sense-organs. I am wearied. Redeem me, O Somanatha.
187.4: I have been bound by the fetters of proverty. I have been damned by the scorching flames of fire of sickness. I have
187.5: I have been extremely distressed by births and deaths, thirst and hunger, Rajas and Tamas. I have been overwhelmed by old age. O lord, see the condition in which I am placed today and be merciful.
187.6: I have been landed in difficulty severally by lust,anger, jealousy, arrogance, vanity and other faults. I have been pierced by them. O lord, like a true leader ward off these enemies of mine.
187.7: I am not virtuous. I am not devout. I am not discreet. I am not merciful. You are a donor. Hence, O lord, worthy of being sought refuge in, place the word 'Soma' in my mind.
187.8: I do not earnestly beg for the overlordship of Devas, O Somanatha. I request humbly for the presence of lotus-like feet of Srisomanatha in the middle of my lotus-like heart.
187.9: Even as I have been known to you as a sinner, listen to my submission. Let me be present always where the word "Siva" is heard.
187.10: O consort of Gauri, O Sankara, O Somanatha, O lord of the universe, O storehouse of sympathy, O soul of all, where eulogies are offered thus, there some happy and successful person is sure to dwell.
187.11: On hearing the eulogy of Dattatreya, Lord Hara was pleased. Bhava, the creator of the universe, said to that Yogin, "I am the bestower of boons".

188.1: There are some other holy centres, viz. ASvattha, Pippala and Mandatirtha in the North. Listen to their excellence.
188.2: Formerly, the saintly lord Agastya of the southern quarter was induced by Devas to make a request to Vindhya mountain.
188.3: I am going on a pilgrimage, O excellent Mountain, along with these sages, the seers of truth. I am going in the southern direction.
188.4: O lord of mountains, give me the way, I beg of you. Accord me a hospitable welcome. Till I return you should stay thus.
188.5: It should not be otherwise. "So be it", said the excel¬ lent mountain surrounded by sages. Sage Agastya went in the southern direction.
188.6: The printed word Bhukti (enjoyment of pleasures) does not fit in the context. Bhakti ( devotiou) seems to be the right word. (Ed.)
188.7: Slowly and slowly he went to GautamI and got initiated for the sacrifice. Surrounded by sages he performed the sacri¬ fice for a year.
188.8: There were two sinful sons of Kaitabha. They were Raksasas, the source of vexation to the virtuous. They were known in the abode of Devas as Asvattha and Pippala.
188.9: Asvattha disguised himself as the holy fig tree and Pippala assumed the form of a brahmin. Both of them were anxious to destroy the sacrifice.
188.10: The evil-minded Danavas assumed the desired forms Asvattha the form of a tree and Pippala the form of a brahmin.
188.11: Both of them harassed brahmins daily, O saint. Who¬ ever touched Aivattha was devoured by that tree.
188.12: Pippala, the younger Raksasa posed, as a chanter of Samans and devoured his disciples. That is why even today the chanters of Samans among the brahmins are devoid of com¬ passion.
188.13: The son of the Sun-god said to the sages: "I shall kill those Raksasas, O brahmins, when I complete my penance. With the penance (as yet) incomplete I am powerless to kill them.*'
188.14: Again, the sages said: "We shall give you the benefit of our penance".
188.15: Saturn, the son of the Sun-god, approached the Raksasa in the form of a holy fig. Saturn was in the guise of a brahmin. As a brahmin he circumambulated the Raksasa.
188.16: As he circumambulated the Raksasa the sinful demon thought that he was an ordinary brahmin. He therefore ate him up by his power of Maya.
188.17: As usual Pippala devoured Saturn, the son of Sun-god. When Saturn-entered his body he looked at the intestines in the belly of the Raksasa.

189.1: The holy centre Somatirtha has also been mentioned by noble men. By taking a holy plunge and by distributing charitable gifts there, the benefit of drinking Soma juice can be had.
189.2: Formerly, the medicinal herbs were the mothers of worlds. They are honoured by all living beings. They are also my divine mothers. They are prior to all prior ones.
189.3: All the ailments are undoubtedly cured by them. Food comes from them and all lives are saved by them. These medicinal herbs are worthy of being honoured by the worlds but being free from egoism they spoke to me.
189.4: O Gautamf, of meritorious waters, O beloved of Sambhu, if you had not come down to the Earth, could the people with miseries arising from their contact with different sins, have found it possible to live?
189.5: Who knows the fate of persons on the Earth, O queen of rivers? O mother Ganga, you are the destroyer of their sins. You are easily accessible to them for ever.
189.6: O Ganga, worthy of being honoured by the three worlds, O mother of the worlds, does anyone understand your real greatness? Although his body is closely embraced by Gauri, lord Siva holds you on his head.

190.1: After getting Moon as their husband, the medicinal herbs became joyous. They spoke these words liked by Ganga and the entire world.
190.2: O king, you redeem him who gifts us on Ganga. You are the excellent one, O lord of herbs. The mobile and immo¬ bile beings are dependent on you.
190.3: The medicinal herbs conversed with king Soma: £t O king you redeem him who gifts us to brahmins.
190.4: We are in the form of Brahman, we are in the form of vital airs. O king, you redeem him who gifts us to brahmins.
190.5: O king, you redeem him who successfully performs holy rites and who gifts us away always to brahmins. It is an adoration unto us.
190.6: O king, you redeem him who gifts away Havya or Kavya which is nectarous and which is consumed or some¬ thing which is weightier.
190.7: O king, you redeem him who devoutly hears, remem¬ bers or reads this episode from the Vedic text."

193.11: Manu (7. 45-48) has given two lists of vyasanas: (1) those arising from lust and (2) those arising from anger. Under the first he enumerates the following fen: hunting, playing the game of dice, sleeping during the day, calu¬ mny, promiscuous intercourse, intoxication, singing, dancing, music and idle rambling. Under the second the following eight are enermerated; deceit or crookedness of temper, rashness, seeking of other's discomfiture, envy, fault¬ finding, robbing of other's money or non-payment of just debts, use of abusive language, and inflicting of harsh punishment.

194.1: I will not survive this. I have become shattered on see¬ ing the splendour and glory of the children of Aditi. I am dejected and am experiencing a peculiarly miserable condition on seeing the excessive prosperity of Aditi. Even if we enter the forest fire it is certainly conducive to happiness. The prosperity and glory of a rival should not be seen even in dream.
194.2: According to Mahclbharata, Adiparvan, Diti, Danu and Aditi were daughters of Daksa Prajapati and were married to Kas'yapa, grandson of Brahma and son of Marici.
194.3: I shall impart to you a holy rite lasting for twelve years. It will yield good fruits. After the holy rite is concluded, I shall impregnate you, as you desire. Ambitions are realized only when one is free from sins.
194.4: O fortunate lady, one should not eat, sneeze or yawn during dawn and dusk when hosts of evil spirits gather together (and are very active).
194.5: These activities should always be pursued, especially laughter, with something to screen it with. You must never stand at the bounding edge of the house during dusk and dawn.
194.6: My beloved one, neither during the day nor at night should one step over the threshing rod, mortar, winnowing basket, pedestal, scabbard and other things.
194.7: One should not lie down with the head towards the north, especially at dusk and dawn. One should never utter a falsehood nor frequent other people's houses.
194.8: No man except one's husband should be looked at wantonly.

194.10: The architect and artificer of the non-gods.
194.11: Once Namuci, the heroic leader of Daityas, saw Indra abandoning the battle and going off. Then he pursued him.
194.12: On seeing him coming Indra became overwhelmed with fear. Leaving off Airavata, Indra entered the foam in water.
194.13: Iam an excellent brahmin, O lord of Daityas. I have come to you as a suppliant after hearing that you are the most distinguished among the donors. Give unto me, a suppliant, the boon sought after.
194.14: Maya took him for a brahmin and said: "It has been given to you by me. When a suppliant is in front, do virtuous persons begin to ponder over (the subject begged for) whether it is too much or too little?"
194.15: Maya went to Indra's abode and intimated everything to him. Indra asked Maya, the expert in Maya, "What am I to do?"
194.16: Out of love Maya gave his Maya to Indra. Indra was then delighted on acquiring it and said "O Maya, what should I do?Tell me that."
194.17: O thunderbolt-armed one, why don't you protect me, your brother. You are desirous of killing me. There is no other greater sin than killing (someone) outside battle.
194.18: (Killing) except in battle (is never just), O lord of large arms. O Indra, fight (with me) when I come out. Hence this is not proper on your part.
194.19: You are the person who has performed a hundred sacrifices; you are the thousand-eyed one, you are the husband of Saci; you are the annihilator of the cities (of enemies); you are the lord ofDevas armed with thunderbolt. O lord this is not proper on your part.
194.20: Or, if you are desirous of a battle, facilitate my com¬ ing out. O thunderbolt-armed one, shun this path.
194.21: In the meantime the patriarch Kasyapa came there. He became distressed on hearing from Agastya about the evil deed of Indra.
194.22: Dear son Indra, come out. Why did you commit this sin? Persons born of pure families do not become inclined to¬ wards sins.
194.23: The thunderbolt-armed one came out and spoke with his face downwards on account of shame. Physiognomy of men itself speaks out their good and bad deeds.
194.24: Even as he eulogized thus, the bull-bannered lord appeared in front of him. He asked Kasyapa, the patriarch, to choose a boon as he pleased.
194.25: No one will ever vanquish Indra when accompanied by Maruts. He will be victorious always. Stay happy for ever, O Patriarch.
194.26: From now onwards if persons commit fratricide unjustly they will meet with extermination of their family as well as other calamities for ever.
194.27: On hearing these words of the lordofDevas, Diti bowed to Sambhu with arms joined in reverence and said:
194.28: If that son happens to be one richly endowed with handsome features, heroism and valour (there is no doubt that he will be more endearing). Even one such son (is endearing). What to say when there are many such (sons)!
194.29: By virtue of your power my sons will be certainly strong and victorious. They are the true sons of the Patriarch and the brothers of Indra.
194.30: O Diti, listen. If persons do not beget sons due to offences committed against the manes or due to the fault of misappropriation of money, the following is the best atonement.
194.31: In such cases the person shall offer balls of rice, pro¬ pitiate manes and gift away a bit of gold. Then he will certainly have a son. The family of these persons does not flourish: those persons who take away or misappropriate money kept in trust, persons who conceal jewels or deny their existence, and those who do not perform the rite of Sraddha.
194.32: This (holy river) shall be the resort of such guilty persons after their death. Children deserving praise shall be born to those living persons who perform pilgrimage to the holy centres.

195.1: As time passed on they begot sons and grandsons. His enemy was the powerful king of birds named Uluka (owl).
195.2: His sons and grandsons were fiery and powerful. Bet¬ ween these two (sets of) birds there was a long-drawn enmity.
195.3: By propitiating Yama and his grandfather Mrtyu, the Pigeon obtained miraculous Yamya weapons and became supe¬ rior to all.
195.4: Similarly, the owl propitiated Fire and became strong. A terrible fight ensued between them as they became excessively arrogant on account of their boons.
195.5: O she-pigeon, this miraculous weapon of mine that has been discharged in the course of the battle is infallible. Where should it be made to rest, O chaste lady. Tell me that.
195.6: Let the miraculous weapon rest in me—neither in my sons nor in my husband. O lord of Havyas, be truthful in speech. O Jatavedas, obeisance be to you.
195.7: In the meantime she-owl saw her husband encircled by the nooses of Yama and struck by his rod. Being distressed and frightened she approached Yama.
195.8: People sympathise (with others) because they are frightened by you. Afraid of you they practise celibacy. Afraid of you, they do good actions. Afraid of you, they scrupulously cling to their duties.
195.9: She spoke to lord Yama: "O lord of the universe, let the nooses hurled by you enter me. Let the rod penetrate me." Thereupon lord Yama sympathetically spoke to her again.
195.10: For the acquisition of virtue and fame and with a desire for the welfare of the worlds, the two birds spoke to the lords well known in the world.

197.1: The mother said to the son: "The king, his wife and the priest, your father, were taken away by a Danava to the nether worlds.**
197.2: While Devas were watching, in the presence of the sacred fires and the brahmins, Mithu the Daitya abducted the king who had been initiated in the sacrifice to the nether worlds along with his wife and the priest.
197.3: Turning his back upon the Rtviks and worshipping the Fire-god, Devapi duly intimated it to the Fire-god. (Then the Fire-god replied.)
197.4: Just like the Rtviks I too am a servant of Devas. I carry Havya to Devas. They are the enjoyers (and therefore) they are the saviours too.
197.5: I shall call Devas and carefully distribute their shares in the Havis to each. Hence, you go hurriedly towards them.
197.6: Devapi approached Devas and bowed to each of them. He then intimated to them the statement of Rtviks, of the Fire-god and (his own threat of) curse.
197.7: When we are invoked by the Vedic Mantras by the Rtviks in the proper order we partake of our shares in the Havis. We are not otherwise free, O excellent brahmin.
197.8: Hence, we are the perpetual followers of the Vedas. We are induced by the Vedas. O brahmin, we are dependent. Therefore, intimate this to the Vedas.
197.9: At the instance of the Vedas the boy Devapi went to Gautami. The brahmin took his bath and having got the proper opportunity eulogized Mahelvara.
197.10: O lord of the chiefs of Devas, I am a mere boy. You are the preceptor of preceptors. I have no power to eulogize you befittingly. Obeisance be to you, O Sambhu.
197.11: The Vedas do not know you. Neither Devas nor sages. Neither Brahma nor Visnu. As you are so you are. Obeisance be to you.
197.12: You protect, O Mahegvara, those who are sinning souls, who are helpless, who are miserable, who are poor and who are sickly.
197.13: The heaven-dwellers who are worshipped by penance, holy rites and Mantras will give them the benefit ordained by you, O lord of the worlds.
197.14: (Even) beggars will turn out to be donors. Whatever they desire is not wanting at your door. You are the cause of this unique situation.
197.15: O preceptor of the universe, O lord, at the mere utter¬ ance of the word Siva, you protect ignorant persons, sinners and those who are immersed in the ocean of hell.
197.16: On hearing the words of Devapi the lord of the uni¬ verse said "So be it". At the behest of Sankara, Devapi got everything.
197.17: Calling Nandin, one of his Ganas, the merciful lord Sambhu sent him with his Spear, O Narada.
197.18: Nandin went to the nether worlds and killed Mithu and the leading Asuras. Bringing his father and others he handed them over to them (Devapi).
197.19: The horse sacrifice of the self-possessed Ar§i§ena was performed there. The Fire-god, Rtviks, Devas, Vedas and sages said:
197.20: Where Sambhu, the lord of Devas, the lord of the uni¬ verse, favourably disposed towards his devotees appeared per¬ sonally, O Devapi, that place has become the holy centre Deva- tlrtha.

198.2: A powerful demon who by the performance of severe penance had secured a boon from Siva and had later became a great terror to gods; killed by Skanda who as a result of a divine planning was bom to Siva and Parvati.

198.8: Eulogize the lord and the goddess. Siva will be pleased with your devotion. Then you will get the fulfilment of cherish¬ ed desires in regard to your children.

198.10: Then the delighted lord Siva, the unchanging and the endless, asked Agni, worshipped by Devas to choose any boon he liked.

198.13: In different places, the holy centres have special marks of recognition. They have separate names as well. It has been briefly mentioned by me.
